FYI, the resetting problem related to this thread has been fixed: https://github.com/r-simmer/simmer/issues/51

2016-05-20 14:48 GMT+02:00 Iñaki Úcar <i.uc...@gmail.com>:
>
> Ok, thanks, I see. Several things here:
> env %>% add_generator("patient", traj, at(rep(0, 10)), mon=2)
>
> run_sim <- function(conf)
> {
>   input <- conf # Change global conf
>   env %>% reset() %>% run(36500) %>% wrap()
>   get_mon_arrivals(env, per_resource = T)
> }
> That wrap() above is useless there, because 1) you are not assigning the result to any variable (wrapped <- env %>% ... %>% wrap()) and 2) you don’t really need it in this case.
> The line input <- conf is NOT changing the global variable input. You are creating a local one with the same name, and the trajectory, as it is defined in a parent scope, uses the parent input, not that one. If you want to change the global input, you need to do input <<- conf. Note the double arrow assignment operator.
> The reset() function is not resetting the generator function, so at(...) generates its 10 arrivals in the first run and that’s it. This is a bug and that’s why you are not getting results in the second run. Thank you, I’ll open an issue and I’ll fix it in the next release. ;-)
>
> In the meantime, the hack #2 should work well. In fact, it’s not a hack at all. I mean, it’s just fine to define a new environment for each new simulation. It’s a hard reset. But in order to be able to use now() inside a trajectory defined in a parent scope, again, you need to use the double arrow assignment:
> run_sim <- function(conf)
> {
>   input <<- conf # Change global conf
>
>   # Redefine the parent environment. This should not complain about anything
>   env <<- simmer("Global Env for now() to work")
>   env %>%
>     add_generator("patient", traj, at(rep(0, 10)), mon=2) %>%
>     add_resource("life", Inf, 0) %>%
>     run(36500) %>% # useless wrap() removed
>     get_mon_arrivals(per_resource = T)
> }
>
> run_sim(TRUE)
>
> run_sim(FALSE)
>
> If you don’t want global variables at all, then you can define the trajectory inside run_sim() and switch back to single arrow assignments.
> ​
>
> 2016-05-19 22:04 GMT+02:00 Shawn Garbett <shawn....@gmail.com>:
> > I don't have a fully working example, but here goes my best attempt at showing what I'm working on:
> >
> > library(simmer)
> >
> > env <- simmer("Global Env for now() to work") # Not used in this example, but main code needs this
> >
> > # Configuration for model run, will be called from another R package with this info
> > # Doing this as a global
> > input <- TRUE
> >
> > # Create some resources
> > env %>% add_resource("life", Inf, 0)
> >
> > # May terminate
> > event <- function(traj)
> > {
> >   traj %>% branch(
> >     function() sample(1:2, 1, prob=c(0.8,0.2)),
> >     merge=c(TRUE,FALSE),
> >     create_trajectory() %>% timeout(1), # Something non-fatal happened
> >     create_trajectory() %>% release("life")
> >   )
> > }
> >
> > traj <- create_trajectory() %>%
> >         seize("life") %>%
> >         branch(function() input+1,
> >                merge=c(FALSE,TRUE),
> >                create_trajectory() %>%
> >                  timeout(40) %>%
> >                  release("life"),
> >                create_trajectory() %>%
> >                  event()
> >         ) %>%
> >         rollback(amount=1, times=100)
> >
> > env %>% add_generator("patient", traj, at(rep(0, 10)), mon=2)
> >
> > run_sim <- function(conf)
> > {
> >   input <- conf # Change global conf
> >   env %>% reset() %>% run(36500) %>% wrap()
> >   get_mon_arrivals(env, per_resource = T)
> > }
> >
> > run_sim(TRUE)
> >
> > run_sim(FALSE) # NO OUTPUT!!!!, doesn't matter if configuration is flipped, the 2nd run is empty
> >
> > # Well that didn't work, now for hacked permutative guessing
> > run_sim <- function(conf)
> > {
> >   input <- conf # Change global conf
> >
> >   env %>% reset()
> >   env %>% add_generator("patient", traj, at(rep(0, 10)), mon=2)
> >   env %>% run(36500) %>% wrap()
> >   get_mon_arrivals(env, per_resource = T)
> > }
> >
> > run_sim(TRUE) # Still no output, probably didn't need to add generator
> >
> > # Hack #2, Seems to work--but does weird things in a larger simulation around resources.
> > run_sim <- function(conf)
> > {
> >   input <- conf # Change global conf
> >
> >   # Blow global environment away!!!
> >   env <- simmer("Global Env for now() to work") # And it complains that it already is defined
> >   env %>% add_generator("patient", traj, at(rep(0, 10)), mon=2)
> >   env %>% add_resource("life", Inf, 0)
> >   env %>% run(36500) %>% wrap()
> >   get_mon_arrivals(env, per_resource = T)
> > }
> >
> > run_sim(TRUE)
> >
> > run_sim(FALSE)
> >
> > Hack #2 appears to work in this example, but at the expense of blowing away the environment. However, in my larger code base, the first model run works great. Then in the Hack #2 run, it doesn't always release resources, even when run with the same input!
> >
> > On Thu, May 19, 2016 at 1:49 PM, Iñaki Úcar <i.uc...@gmail.com> wrote:
> > > I don't understand the problem. Could you provide us with a brief example, please?
> > >
> > > 2016-05-19 20:36 GMT+02:00 Shawn Garbett <shawn....@gmail.com>:
> > > > This is proving to be a problem for me. 'env' as a global variable is now forcing my model inputs to be a global as well.
> > > >
> > > > I have a list of "inputs". These control trajectory behavior through permutations to compare. So, I wrote a function where the patient trajectory is a function of inputs. Now, if I reset the global env, the generator's that were added are still present. The only solution is to now make inputs a global variable as well, since I can't way to delete a previously defined generator.
> > > >
> > > > So, now 'env' and 'inputs' are now forced to be global objects. I prefer a more functional approach that doesn't depend on environment globals.
> > > >
> > > > The best solution to all this is if there was a 'now()' function that worked in a trajectory and it didn't depend on accessing a global variable.

messages.subject: Renege
messages.subject_clean: Renege
messages.body_plain:
Is there an obvious way for arrivals to renege?

It's related to this issue: https://github.com/r-simmer/simmer/issues/49, but with the important difference that reneging occurs between entering a queue and being served, rather than when rejected from a finite queue.  There's a SimPy example "Reneging (or abandoning) customers" here: https://pythonhosted.org/SimPy/Tutorials/TheBank2.html.

I don't think this can be implemented by branching, but you might have a genius suggestion.

messages.subject: Issue resetting arrival times between each rep
messages.subject_clean: Issue resetting arrival times between each rep
messages.body_plain:
I am modeling a hair salon where the arrival rates vary by hour.  I have written a function helper function that outputs a dataframe(sched) of entities whose inter arrival times reflect those varying rates.

I use the schedule with a generator with this code -

add_generator("customer", t0, function() sched$IAT[(get_n_generated(envs, "customer")) + 1] , mon = 2)

I tried to replicate using lapply, with this code -

envsRep <- lapply(1:reps, function(i) {
        sched <- schedIt() #makes the IATs
        envs %>% run(until=730)
})

My intention is to have a new schedule generate at each replication.  However the arrival data shows each replication having the same arrival times - clearly implying that the generator is not 'resetting' when the sched object is recreated.

Is there a way to make this work? All ideas appreciated.

--
“The time will come when diligent research over long periods will bring to light things which now lie hidden."

messages.subject_clean: [simmer-devel] Issue resetting arrival times between each rep
messages.body_plain:
If arrivals are driven by an exponential distribution, this is "memoryless". I.e., you could draw arrivals based on this, then at some point redraw events that haven't occurred yet. So, one could have an event occurring on a set time that triggers a redraw. If the rates change at that point, it works out fine.

I'm driving our simulations via a main event loop. See: https://github.com/spgarbet/right/blob/master/simvastatin/simvastatin.R

This works since most of our events are exponential in our models.

messages.subject: Re: [simmer-devel] Issue resetting arrival times between each rep
messages.subject_clean: [simmer-devel] Issue resetting arrival times between each rep
messages.body_plain:
My approach is based on exponential draws, but as it is a non-stationary process the rate (and mean of the exp dist) changes each hour to best match the real world data on clientele - ie I need on average the same number of arrivals per hour that the store did. I addressed this by drawing across the whole sim time at the highest rate, and then thinning the the remaining hours (code below).  The goal here is to have the right number of people arriving in each hour - this can't easily be accomplished by changing the rate on the hour as it is possible to skip part of the busy period.  I'm definitely interested in an example that makes this work however.

I confess that I don't fully understand what you mean by main event loop.  I also see only the one generator in your code which appears to be regular.

Is it possible to reset the generator between replications?

schedIt <- function() {

        ##Here is where you can do a given day or month etc
        ##It is now the average by hour irrespectice of day
        rates <- byHour

        rates <- rbind(rates[12,], rates[1:11,]) #gets things in the right order - 10 am was at the end for some reaosn
        maxRate <- max(rates$clients)

        ##Make a lot first - ~100 hours worth
        denseGen <- rexp(12000,rate=(1/maxRate))

        ##Converts IAT into time of day
        clockSched <- as.numeric()
        temp <- 0
        for(i in 1:length(denseGen)) {
                clockSched <- c(clockSched, temp+denseGen[i])
                temp <- temp+denseGen[i]
        }

        ##Takes only the ones that happen before closing
        clockSched <- clockSched[clockSched < 720]

        ##'Thins' the values to match the probalities by hour
        rem <- as.numeric()
        startTime <- 0
        endTime <- 60
        for(hour in 1:nrow(rates)) {
                rate <- rates$clients[hour]
                #print(rate)
                for(i in 1:length(clockSched)) {
                        #print(i)
                        test <- runif(1,0:1) > rate/maxRate
                        #print(test)
                        if(clockSched[i] >= startTime & clockSched[i] < endTime) {
                                if(test){rem <- c(rem,i) } }

                }
                startTime <- startTime + 60
                endTime <- endTime + 60
        }

        ##Removes the values from the clock schedule
        clockSched <- clockSched[-rem]

        ##converts the clock time back to an updated IAT after 'thinning'
        temp <- 0
        IAT <- as.numeric()
        for(i in 1:length(clockSched)){
                IAT <- c(IAT,clockSched[i]-temp)
                temp <- clockSched[i]
        }

        ##Bookkeeping to make a data frame
        id <- seq(1,length(clockSched))
        sched <- cbind(id,clockSched,IAT)
        sched <- data.frame(sched)

        return(sched)

}

Check out the introductory vignette, replication section <http://r-simmer.org/docs/vignettes/A-introduction.html#replication>. In your lapply, you are running the same simulator multiple times, but you want multiple simulators (multiple replicas), so you need to embed the whole simulator’s definition inside this lapply. Something like this should do the trick:

envsRep <- lapply(1:reps, function(i) {
  sched <- schedIt() #makes the IATs

  env %>% simmer() %>%
    ...
    add_generator("customer", t0, function() sched$IAT[(get_n_generated(env, "customer")) + 1] , mon = 2)
  env %>% run(until=730)
})

messages.body_plain:
If it's arrivals, Iñaki snippet shows the way.

It helps to understand the relationship between exponential distribution and Poisson processes.

First the memoryless property demonstration:

> x <- rexp(1000)
> y <- x
> n <- length(y[x > 1])
> y[x > 1] <- rexp(n) + 1
> hist(x)
> hist(y)

x is a random exponential draw.
y is a redraw for all events that are greater than 1.

When plotted, there is little difference between the two. A ks.test shouldn't be able to tell the difference (if it does it's a type I error).

So, let's say you're going to simulate 3 hours.

During hour 1, 10 people arrive, or 10 per hour
During hour 2, 50 people arrive, or 50 per hour
During hour 3, 20 people arrive, or 20 per hour.

Generating on demand as Iñaki shows will work, but one must be careful with the borders.

The naive approach ignoring the borders would be as follows:

new_rate <- function(sim_t)
{
  if(sim_t <= 1.0) rexp(1, 10)
  else if(sim_t <= 2.0) rexp(1, 50)
  else if(sim_t <= 3.0) rexp(1, 20)
  else stop("out of sim range")
}

With this a draw at sim_t 0.99 would overlap the 10 per hour rate into hour 2. With a very slow rate transitioning to a fast one, this could impact the simulation. So a little more caution is required with boundary conditions:

new_rate <- function(sim_t)
{
   draw <- if(sim_t <= 1.0) rexp(1, 10)
                else if(sim_t <= 2.0) rexp(1, 50)
                else if(sim_t <= 3.0) rexp(1, 20)
                else stop("out of sim range")

  # Boundary checks
  if(sim_t <= 1.0 && sim_t + draw > 1.0) draw <- sim_t + rexp(1, 50)
  if(sim_t >= 1.0 && sim_t <= 2.0 && sim_t+draw > 2.0) draw <- sim_t + rexp(1,20)
  if(draw > 3.0) draw <- (-1)  # No more

  draw
}

This properly shifts the rates at the boundary, using the memoryless property of the exponential distribution.

Just realized I got it wrong. Boundaries are tricky! I think this is what was intended....

new_rate <- function(sim_t)
{
   draw <- if(sim_t <= 1.0) rexp(1, 10)
                else if(sim_t <= 2.0) rexp(1, 50)
                else if(sim_t <= 3.0) rexp(1, 20)
                else stop("out of sim range")

  # Boundary checks

  if(sim_t <= 1.0 && sim_t + draw > 1.0) draw <- (1.0 - sim_t) + rexp(1, 50)
  if(sim_t >= 1.0 && sim_t <= 2.0 && sim_t+draw > 2.0) draw <- (2.0 - sim_t) + rexp(1,20)

  if(draw > 3.0) draw <- (-1)  # No more

  draw
}

messages.subject_clean: scheduling infinite capacity and instantaneously
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

Iñaki was quite right on Twitter, it is possible to schedule a single, persistent change in capacity.  Sorry about that.

It's also possible to schedule infinite capacity, though the results of get_mon_arrivals show a subtle difference when you use `Inf` capacity vs some large number.  Compare schedule1 and schedule2 below.

When scheduling an infinite server to open instantaneously and then immediately shut -- basically a gate that opens from time to time to let the existing queue pass through, then this only works for a large capacity, not an `Inf` capacity.  Compare schedule3 and schedule4 below.  It's a bit of a hack, but I used it to implement the wait-event SimPy example here: https://github.com/nacnudus/simmer-bank/blob/master/18-waitevent.R

``` r
library(simmer)

arrival <-
  create_trajectory("Arrival trajectory") %>%
  seize("server") %>%
  release("server")

# These two both work, but aren't quite the same.  Both are technically correct,
# though -- my mistake.
schedule1 <- schedule(c(3, 100), c(999, 0))
schedule2 <- schedule(c(3, 100), c(Inf, 0))

# These are designed to implement a gate that opens instantaneously every
# period, and shuts immediately.  Only the first version works.
schedule3 <- schedule(c(3, 3), c(Inf, 0), period = 3)
schedule4 <- schedule(c(3, 3), c(999, 0), period = 3)

## Model/Experiment ------------------------------

set.seed(393939)
env <-
  simmer() %>%
  add_resource("server", capacity = schedule1) %>%
  add_generator("Arrival", arrival, at(1:9))
env %>% run(until = 12)
#> simmer environment: anonymous | now: 100 | next:
#> { Resource: server | monitored: 1 | server status: 0(0) | queue status: 0(Inf) }
#> { Generator: Arrival | monitored: 1 | n_generated: 9 }
```

Hi Cameron,

This is because only `amount` is allowed to be a function. Certainly, we should document this better. If it's interesting, we can extend this functionality to `priority`, and even to `preemptible` and `restart`. To all: what do you think?

Meanwhile, if your set of priorities is finite, you can implement this using a branch with multiple trajectories, one for each priority.

messages.subject: need your opinion: cancer center scenario
messages.subject_clean: need your opinion: cancer center scenario
messages.body_plain:
Dear Experts, need your opinion..

A center for treatment of leukemia has only 30 beds

Treatment involves the following process:

Induction 1--> Induction 2 --> Consolidation 1 --> Consolidation 2

Step #1 --> Induction 1

-accepting new cases to receive Chemotherapy Known as Induction 1 Regimen

-rate of arrival 2.3 patients / week

-average length of stay (ALOS) = 31 days

Step #2 -->  Induction 2

-84.2 % of patients from step #1 arrive successfully to this step

-ALOS = 28 days

-highest priority for admission

Step #3  --> Consolidation 1

-74.6% of patients from step#1 arrive successfully to this step

-ALOS = 25 days

- priority for admission less than step#2 but higher than step#1

Step #4 --> Consolidation 2

-73.5% of patients from step#1 arrive successfully to this step

-ALOS = 31.5 days

- priority for admission less than step#2 but higher than step#1

Using the R-script below, running the simulation for 2 years (730 days) and 30 beds gave the following

server status: 30(30) | queue status: 42
> mean(x$queue)
[1] 22.3562

Using the R-script below, running the simulation for 2 years (730 days) and 31 beds gave the following
server status: 31(31) | queue status: 13
> mean(x$queue)
[1] 6.314767

Using the R-script below, running the simulation for 2 years (730 days) and 32 beds gave the following
server status: 30(32) | queue status: 0
> mean(x$queue)
[1] 0.57

Does this mean that: "if I increase the center capacity from 30 to 32 beds, I will have no waiting list?"

========================= R Script ==============================

library(simmer)

# rate of new patient arrival = 2.3 per week
# inter-arrival time (IAT)= 7/2.3 days

#rn = interarrival time of new cases who will receive Induction 1
rn <- 7/2.3 # IAT = 7/2.3, Priority = 1

#rind2 = interarrival time of patients who will receive Induction 2
rind2 <- (1/0.842) * rn # priority = 9

#consol1 = interarrival time of patients who will receive consolidation 1
rconsol1 <- (1/0.746) * rn # priority = 8

#consol1 = interarrival time of patients who will receive consolidation 2
rconsol2 <- (1/0.735) * rn # priority = 8

env <- simmer("AML-env")

## add a new patient trajectory
newpatient <- create_trajectory("newAMLpatientpath") %>%

  seize("bed", amount = 1, priority = 1) %>%
  ## 31 day
  timeout(function() rnorm(1, 31, 2)) %>%
  release("bed", 1)

## add a Induction2 patient trajectory
rind2patient <- create_trajectory("rind2AMLpatientpath") %>%
  seize("bed", amount = 1, priority = 9) %>%
  ## 28 days
  timeout(function() rnorm(1, 28, 2)) %>%
  release("bed", 1)

## add a Consolidation1 patient trajectory
consol1patient <- create_trajectory("consol1AMLpatientpath") %>%
    seize("bed", amount = 1, priority = 8) %>%
  ## 25 days
  timeout(function() rnorm(1, 25, 2)) %>%
  release("bed", 1)

## add a Consolidation2 patient trajectory
consol2patient <- create_trajectory("consol2AMLpatientpath") %>%
    seize("bed", amount = 1, priority = 8) %>%
  ## 31.5 days
  timeout(function() rnorm(1, 31.5, 2)) %>%
  release("bed", 1)

env %>%
  add_resource("bed", 30) %>%
  add_generator("newpatient", newpatient, function() rn) %>%
  add_generator("rind2patient", rind2patient, function() rind2) %>%
  add_generator("consol1patient", consol1patient, function() rconsol1) %>%
  add_generator("consol2patient", consol2patient, function() rconsol2)

env %>% run(until=730) ## run for two years (365 * 2 = 730)
x<-env %>% get_mon_resources()
y<-env %>% get_mon_arrivals()
mean(x$queue)

> Does this mean that: "if I increase the center capacity from 30 to 32 beds, I will have no waiting list?"

It would, if the model were good, but it doesn't seem reasonable to me.
You have no arrival process. You've merely assigned constant IATs.
Patients from the first stage don't go through subsequent stages. Instead, you are generating new different arrivals for each stage (!).

messages.body_plain:
You could built one trajectory to describe your simulation problem. Have look at the branching tactics described in https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/simmer/vignettes/C-trajectories.html#branch. From a branch statement you can then model when and how you move towards a subtrajectory (e.g. the "74.6% of patients from step#1 arrive successfully to this step" statements).

Between each step you can use a timeout where you wait an appropriate amount of time between e.g. step 1 and step 2. Once the timeout is over, you can let the patient re-seize a bed (and it will compete here with other patients that might be in a different step). You can of course also work with priorities in the seize, to give different patients at different stages different priorities at seizing a bed (which is probably realistic)

please check the following modified script with branches, your feedback is highly appreciated...

library(simmer)

# rate of new patient arrival = 2.3 per week

# interarrival time (IAT)= 7/2.3 days

env <- simmer("AML-env")

## add a new patient trajectory
newpatient <- create_trajectory("newAMLpatientpath") %>%

  branch(function() sample(c(1,2),size=1,replace=F,prob=c(0.999,0.001)), merge=c(T, T),
         create_trajectory("Induction1") %>%

           seize("bed", amount = 1, priority = 1) %>%

           seize("Induction1_in", amount = 1, priority = 1) %>%

           ## 31 day
           timeout(function() rnorm(1, 31, 2)) %>%

           release("bed", 1)%>%

           #================ Induction 2
           branch(function() sample(c(1,2),size=1,replace=F,prob=c(0.842,0.158)), merge=c(T, T),
                  create_trajectory("Induction2") %>%

                    seize("bed", amount = 1, priority = 9) %>%

                    seize("Induction2_in", amount = 1, priority = 9) %>%
                    ## 28 day

                    timeout(function() rnorm(1, 28, 2)) %>%

                    release("bed", 1)%>%
                    #=============== Consolidation 1
                    branch(function() sample(c(1,2),size=1,replace=F,prob=c(0.746,0.254)), merge=c(T, T),
                           create_trajectory("Consolidation1") %>%

                             seize("bed", amount = 1, priority = 8) %>%

                             seize("Consolidation1_in", amount = 1, priority = 8) %>%
                             ## 25 day

                             timeout(function() rnorm(1, 25, 2)) %>%

                             release("bed", 1) %>%
                             #===============Consolidation 2
                             branch(function() sample(c(1,2),size=1,replace=F,prob=c(0.99,0.01)), merge=c(T, T),
                                    create_trajectory("Consolidation2") %>%

                                      seize("bed", amount = 1, priority = 8) %>%

                                      seize("Consolidation2_in", amount = 1, priority = 8) %>%
                                      ## 31.5 day

                                      timeout(function() rnorm(1, 31.5, 2)) %>%
                                      release("bed", 1)

                                    ,
                                    create_trajectory("Consolidation2_out") %>%
                                      seize("Consolidation2_out", amount = 1, priority = 1)

                             )
                           #=============End Consolidation2
                           ,
                           create_trajectory("Consolidation1_out") %>%
                             seize("Consolidation1_out", amount = 1, priority = 1)

                    )
                  #===============End Consolidation 1
                  ,
                  create_trajectory("Induction2_out") %>%
                    seize("Induction2_out", amount = 1, priority = 1)

           )
         #=================End Induction 2

         ,
         create_trajectory("Induction1_out") %>%
           seize("Induction1_out", amount = 1, priority = 1)

  )

env %>%

  ## add true resource
  add_resource("bed", 20) %>%

  ## add resources for counting purpose
  add_resource("Induction1_in", Inf) %>%
  add_resource("Induction2_in", Inf) %>%
  add_resource("Consolidation1_in", Inf) %>%
  add_resource("Consolidation2_in", Inf) %>%

  add_resource("Induction1_out", Inf) %>%
  add_resource("Induction2_out", Inf) %>%
  add_resource("Consolidation1_out", Inf) %>%
  add_resource("Consolidation2_out", Inf) %>%

  add_generator("newpatient", newpatient, function() rnorm(1, mean=3.33, sd=0.5))

env %>% run(until=730) ## run for two years (365 * 2 = 730)
x<-env %>% get_mon_resources()
y<-env %>% get_mon_arrivals()

z<-env %>% get_mon_attributes()

plot_resource_utilization(env, c("bed"))

write.csv(y,"y.csv")
mean(x$queue)
arrivals <- get_mon_arrivals(env, per_resource = T)
write.csv(arrivals,"arrivals.csv")

Dear Iñaki

thanks a lot for your efforts and support

regarding queue, I mean percentage of queue from each stage: how many patients are waiting for Induction1, how many for Induction2, how many for Consolidation1 and consolidation2. All what I get is total number in queue.

one more thing, is my model OK now or do you still see something that needs improvement?

On Thursday, 9 June 2016, Iñaki Úcar <i.uc...@gmail.com> wrote:

> What do you mean by "breakdown the queue"?
> El 9/6/2016 8:55, "Mohamed Kamal" <mohamedk...@gmail.com> escribió:
> > I also need to know if there is a way to breakdown the queue.
> > thanks again in advance.
> >
> > On Thursday, 9 June 2016, Mohamed Kamal <mohamedk...@gmail.com> wrote:
> > > please check the following modified script with branches, your feedback is highly appreciated...
> > >
> > > library(simmer)
> > >
> > > # rate of new patient arrival = 2.3 per week
> > >
> > > # interarrival time (IAT)= 7/2.3 days
> > >
> > > env <- simmer("AML-env")
> > >
> > > ## add a new patient trajectory
> > > newpatient <- create_trajectory("newAMLpatientpath") %>%
> > >   branch(function() sample(c(1,2),size=1,replace=F,prob=c(0.999,0.001)), merge=c(T, T),
> > >          create_trajectory("Induction1") %>%
> > >            seize("bed", amount = 1, priority = 1) %>%
> > >            seize("Induction1_in", amount = 1, priority = 1) %>%
> > >            ## 31 day
> > >            timeout(function() rnorm(1, 31, 2)) %>%
> > >            release("bed", 1)%>%
> > >
> > >            #================ Induction 2
> > >            branch(function() sample(c(1,2),size=1,replace=F,prob=c(0.842,0.158)), merge=c(T, T),
> > >                   create_trajectory("Induction2") %>%
> > >                     seize("bed", amount = 1, priority = 9) %>%
> > >                     seize("Induction2_in", amount = 1, priority = 9) %>%
> > >                     ## 28 day
> > >                     timeout(function() rnorm(1, 28, 2)) %>%
> > >                     release("bed", 1)%>%
> > >                     #=============== Consolidation 1
> > >                     branch(function() sample(c(1,2),size=1,replace=F,prob=c(0.746,0.254)), merge=c(T, T),
> > >                            create_trajectory("Consolidation1") %>%
> > >                              seize("bed", amount = 1, priority = 8) %>%
> > >                              seize("Consolidation1_in", amount = 1, priority = 8) %>%
> > >                              ## 25 day
> > >                              timeout(function() rnorm(1, 25, 2)) %>%
> > >                              release("bed", 1) %>%
> > >                              #===============Consolidation 2
> > >                              branch(function() sample(c(1,2),size=1,replace=F,prob=c(0.99,0.01)), merge=c(T, T),
> > >                                     create_trajectory("Consolidation2") %>%
> > >                                       seize("bed", amount = 1, priority = 8) %>%
> > >                                       seize("Consolidation2_in", amount = 1, priority = 8) %>%
> > >                                       ## 31.5 day
> > >                                       timeout(function() rnorm(1, 31.5, 2)) %>%
> > >                                       release("bed", 1)
> > >                                     ,
> > >                                     create_trajectory("Consolidation2_out") %>%
> > >                                       seize("Consolidation2_out", amount = 1, priority = 1)
> > >
> > >                              )
> > >                            #=============End Consolidation2
> > >                            ,
> > >                            create_trajectory("Consolidation1_out") %>%
> > >                              seize("Consolidation1_out", amount = 1, priority = 1)
> > >
> > >                     )
> > >                   #===============End Consolidation 1
> > >                   ,
> > >                   create_trajectory("Induction2_out") %>%
> > >                     seize("Induction2_out", amount = 1, priority = 1)
> > >
> > >            )
> > >          #=================End Induction 2
> > >
> > >          ,
> > >          create_trajectory("Induction1_out") %>%
> > >            seize("Induction1_out", amount = 1, priority = 1)
> > >
> > >   )
> > >
> > > env %>%
> > >
> > >   ## add true resource
> > >   add_resource("bed", 20) %>%
> > >
> > >   ## add resources for counting purpose
> > >   add_resource("Induction1_in", Inf) %>%
> > >   add_resource("Induction2_in", Inf) %>%
> > >   add_resource("Consolidation1_in", Inf) %>%
> > >   add_resource("Consolidation2_in", Inf) %>%
> > >
> > >   add_resource("Induction1_out", Inf) %>%
> > >   add_resource("Induction2_out", Inf) %>%
> > >   add_resource("Consolidation1_out", Inf) %>%
> > >   add_resource("Consolidation2_out", Inf) %>%
> > >
> > >
> > >   add_generator("newpatient", newpatient, function() rnorm(1, mean=3.33, sd=0.5))
> > >
> > > env %>% run(until=730) ## run for two years (365 * 2 = 730)
> > > x<-env %>% get_mon_resources()
> > > y<-env %>% get_mon_arrivals()
> > > z<-env %>% get_mon_attributes()
> > >
> > >
> > > plot_resource_utilization(env, c("bed"))
> > >
> > > write.csv(y,"y.csv")
> > > mean(x$queue)
> > > arrivals <- get_mon_arrivals(env, per_resource = T)
> > > write.csv(arrivals,"arrivals.csv")
> > >
> > >
> > > On Wednesday, June 8, 2016 at 12:43:12 AM UTC+2, mokoka...@gmail.com wrote:
> > > >
> > > > Dear Experts, need your opinion..
> > > >
> > > >
> > > > A center for treatment of leukemia has only 30 beds
> > > >
> > > >
> > > > Treatment involves the following process:
> > > >
> > > > Induction 1--> Induction 2 --> Consolidation 1 --> Consolidation 2
> > > >
> > > >
> > > > Step #1 --> Induction 1
> > > >
> > > > -accepting new cases to receive Chemotherapy Known as Induction 1 Regimen
> > > >
> > > > -rate of arrival 2.3 patients / week
> > > >
> > > > -average length of stay (ALOS) = 31 days
> > > >
> > > >
> > > > Step #2 -->  Induction 2
> > > >
> > > > -84.2 % of patients from step #1 arrive successfully to this step
> > > >
> > > > -ALOS = 28 days
> > > >
> > > > -highest priority for admission
> > > >
> > > >
> > > > Step #3  --> Consolidation 1
> > > >
> > > > -74.6% of patients from step#1 arrive successfully to this step
> > > >
> > > > -ALOS = 25 days
> > > >
> > > > - priority for admission less than step#2 but higher than step#1
> > > >
> > > >
> > > > Step #4 --> Consolidation 2
> > > >
> > > > -73.5% of patients from step#1 arrive successfully to this step
> > > >
> > > > -ALOS = 31.5 days
> > > >
> > > > - priority for admission less than step#2 but higher than step#1
> > > >
> > > >
> > > >
> > > > Using the R-script below, running the simulation for 2 years (730 days) and 30 beds gave the following
> > > >
> > > > server status: 30(30) | queue status: 42
> > > > > mean(x$queue)
> > > > [1] 22.3562
> > > >
> > > >
> > > >
> > > > Using the R-script below, running the simulation for 2 years (730 days) and 31 beds gave the following
> > > > server status: 31(31) | queue status: 13
> > > > > mean(x$queue)
> > > > [1] 6.314767
> > > >
> > > >
> > > >
> > > > Using the R-script below, running the simulation for 2 years (730 days) and 32 beds gave the following
> > > > server status: 30(32) | queue status: 0
> > > > > mean(x$queue)
> > > > [1] 0.57
> > > >
> > > > Does this mean that: "if I increase the center capacity from 30 to 32 beds, I will have no waiting list?"
> > > >
> > > > ========================= R Script ==============================
> > > >
> > > >
> > > > library(simmer)
> > > >
> > > > # rate of new patient arrival = 2.3 per week
> > > > # inter-arrival time (IAT)= 7/2.3 days
> > > >
> > > > #rn = interarrival time of new cases who will receive Induction 1
> > > > rn <- 7/2.3 # IAT = 7/2.3, Priority = 1
> > > >
> > > > #rind2 = interarrival time of patients who will receive Induction 2
> > > > rind2 <- (1/0.842) * rn # priority = 9
> > > >
> > > > #consol1 = interarrival time of patients who will receive consolidation 1
> > > > rconsol1 <- (1/0.746) * rn # priority = 8
> > > >
> > > > #consol1 = interarrival time of patients who will receive consolidation 2
> > > > rconsol2 <- (1/0.735) * rn # priority = 8
> > > >
> > > > env <- simmer("AML-env")
> > > >
> > > > ## add a new patient trajectory
> > > > newpatient <- create_trajectory("newAMLpatientpath") %>%
> > > >
> > > >   seize("bed", amount = 1, priority = 1) %>%
> > > >   ## 31 day
> > > >   timeout(function() rnorm(1, 31, 2)) %>%
> > > >   release("bed", 1)
> > > >
> > > > ## add a Induction2 patient trajectory
> > > > rind2patient <- create_trajectory("rind2AMLpatientpath") %>%
> > > >   seize("bed", amount = 1, priority = 9) %>%
> > > >   ## 28 days
> > > >   timeout(function() rnorm(1, 28, 2)) %>%
> > > >   release("bed", 1)
> > > >
> > > > ## add a Consolidation1 patient trajectory
> > > > consol1patient <- create_trajectory("consol1AMLpatientpath") %>%
> > > >     seize("bed", amount = 1, priority = 8) %>%
> > > >   ## 25 days
> > > >   timeout(function() rnorm(1, 25, 2)) %>%
> > > >   release("bed", 1)
> > > >
> > > > ## add a Consolidation2 patient trajectory
> > > > consol2patient <- create_trajectory("consol2AMLpatientpath") %>%
> > > >     seize("bed", amount = 1, priority = 8) %>%
> > > >   ## 31.5 days
> > > >   timeout(function() rnorm(1, 31.5, 2)) %>%
> > > >   release("bed", 1)
> > > >
> > > > env %>%
> > > >   add_resource("bed", 30) %>%
> > > >   add_generator("newpatient", newpatient, function() rn) %>%
> > > >   add_generator("rind2patient", rind2patient, function() rind2) %>%
> > > >   add_generator("consol1patient", consol1patient, function() rconsol1) %>%
> > > >   add_generator("consol2patient", consol2patient, function() rconsol2)
> > > >
> > > > env %>% run(until=730) ## run for two years (365 * 2 = 730)
> > > > x<-env %>% get_mon_resources()
> > > > y<-env %>% get_mon_arrivals()
> > > > mean(x$queue)
> > >

> > > > > mean(x$queue)

> > > > > > Dear Experts, need your opinion..
> > > > > >
> > > > > >
> > > > > > A center for treatment of leukemia has only 30 beds
> > > > > >
> > > > > >
> > > > > > Treatment involves the following process:
> > > > > >
> > > > > > Induction 1--> Induction 2 --> Consolidation 1 --> Consolidation 2
> > > > > >
> > > > > >
> > > > > > Step #1 --> Induction 1
> > > > > >
> > > > > > -accepting new cases to receive Chemotherapy Known as Induction 1 Regimen
> > > > > >
> > > > > > -rate of arrival 2.3 patients / week
> > > > > >
> > > > > > -average length of stay (ALOS) = 31 days
> > > > > >
> > > > > >
> > > > > > Step #2 -->  Induction 2
> > > > > >
> > > > > > -84.2 % of patients from step #1 arrive successfully to this step
> > > > > >
> > > > > > -ALOS = 28 days
> > > > > >
> > > > > > -highest priority for admission
> > > > > >
> > > > > >
> > > > > > Step #3  --> Consolidation 1
> > > > > >
> > > > > > -74.6% of patients from step#1 arrive successfully to this step
> > > > > >
> > > > > > -ALOS = 25 days
> > > > > >
> > > > > > - priority for admission less than step#2 but higher than step#1
> > > > > >
> > > > > >
> > > > > > Step #4 --> Consolidation 2
> > > > > >
> > > > > > -73.5% of patients from step#1 arrive successfully to this step
> > > > > >
> > > > > > -ALOS = 31.5 days
> > > > > >
> > > > > > - priority for admission less than step#2 but higher than step#1
> > > > > >
> > > > > >
> > > > > >
> > > > > > Using the R-script below, running the simulation for 2 years (730 days) and 30 beds gave the following
> > > > > >
> > > > > > server status: 30(30) | queue status: 42
> > > > > > > mean(x$queue)
> > > > > > [1] 22.3562
> > > > > >
> > > > > >
> > > > > >
> > > > > > Using the R-script below, running the simulation for 2 years (730 days) and 31 beds gave the following
> > > > > > server status: 31(31) | queue status: 13
> > > > > > > mean(x$queue)
> > > > > > [1] 6.314767
> > > > > >
> > > > > >
> > > > > >
> > > > > > Using the R-script below, running the simulation for 2 years (730 days) and 32 beds gave the following
> > > > > > server status: 30(32) | queue status: 0
> > > > > > > mean(x$queue)
> > > > > > [1] 0.57
> > > > > >
> > > > > > Does this mean that: "if I increase the center capacity from 30 to 32 beds, I will have no waiting list?"
> > > > > >
> > > > > > ========================= R Script ==============================
> > > > > >
> > > > > >
> > > > > > library(simmer)
> > > > > >
> > > > > > # rate of new patient arrival = 2.3 per week
> > > > > > # inter-arrival time (IAT)= 7/2.3 days
> > > > > >
> > > > > > #rn = interarrival time of new cases who will receive Induction 1
> > > > > > rn <- 7/2.3 # IAT = 7/2.3, Priority = 1
> > > > > >
> > > > > > #rind2 = interarrival time of patients who will receive Induction 2
> > > > > > rind2 <- (1/0.842) * rn # priority = 9
> > > > > >
> > > > > > #consol1 = interarrival time of patients who will receive consolidation 1
> > > > > > rconsol1 <- (1/0.746) * rn # priority = 8
> > > > > >
> > > > > > #consol1 = interarrival time of patients who will receive consolidation 2
> > > > > > rconsol2 <- (1/0.735) * rn # priority = 8
> > > > > >
> > > > > > env <- simmer("AML-env")
> > > > > >
> > > > > > ## add a new patient trajectory
> > > > > > newpatient <- create_trajectory("newAMLpatientpath") %>%
> > > > > >
> > > > > >   seize("bed", amount = 1, priority = 1) %>%
> > > > > >   ## 31 day
> > > > > >   timeout(function() rnorm(1, 31, 2)) %>%
> > > > > >   release("bed", 1)
> > > > > >
> > > > > > ## add a Induction2 patient trajectory
> > > > > > rind2patient <- create_trajectory("rind2AMLpatientpath") %>%
> > > > > >   seize("bed", amount = 1, priority = 9) %>%
> > > > > >   ## 28 days
> > > > > >   timeout(function() rnorm(1, 28, 2)) %>%
> > > > > >   release("bed", 1)
> > > > > >
> > > > > > ## add a Consolidation1 patient trajectory
> > > > > > consol1patient <- create_trajectory("consol1AMLpatientpath") %>%
> > > > > >     seize("bed", amount = 1, priority = 8) %>%
> > > > > >   ## 25 days
> > > > > >   timeout(function() rnorm(1, 25, 2)) %>%
> > > > > >   release("bed", 1)
> > > > > >
> > > > > > ## add a Consolidation2 patient trajectory

> > > > > >     seize("bed", amount = 1, priority = 8) %>%
> > > > > >   ## 31.5 days
> > > > > >   timeout(function() rnorm(1, 31.5, 2)) %>%

> > > > > >
> > > > > > env %>%
> > > > > >   add_resource("bed", 30) %>%
> > > > > >   add_generator("newpatient", newpatient, function() rn) %>%
> > > > > >   add_generator("rind2patient", rind2patient, function() rind2) %>%
> > > > > >   add_generator("consol1patient", consol1patient, function() rconsol1) %>%
> > > > > >   add_generator("consol2patient", consol2patient, function() rconsol2)
> > > > > >
> > > > > > env %>% run(until=730) ## run for two years (365 * 2 = 730)
> > > > > > x<-env %>% get_mon_resources()
> > > > > > y<-env %>% get_mon_arrivals()
> > > > > > mean(x$queue)

Op donderdag 9 juni 201

messages.body_plain:
I think I dont "need" to label beds, just asking if it is possible to do it.
So, do you think this model is OK ? I mean, if the percentages are matching reality, shall i depend on it to predict scenarios?

On Friday, 10 June 2016, Bart Smeets <bartsm...@gmail.com> wrote:

> Can you explain why you want to label the beds in this case? If the first free bed will always be seized, won't the final results be the comparable to the output you have now?
>
> Op donderdag 9 juni 2016 15:39:36 UTC+2 schreef Mohamed Kamal:

> > Experts
> >
> > need your advice, is it possible to label Beds as Bed01, Bed02 ,....., Bed30

> > and when the patient try to seize "loop" through the beds and choose the first free bed
> >
> > On Thursday, June 9, 2016 at 11:56:00 AM UTC+2, Mohamed Kamal wrote:

> > > @Bart Smeet
> > > any feedback
> > >
> > > On Thursday, June 9, 2016 at 11:50:51 AM UTC+2, Iñaki Úcar wrote:

> > > > Sorry, I can't take a look at your code until tomorrow.

> > > > 2016-06-09 10:45 GMT+02:00 Mohamed Kamal

> > > > > Dear Iñaki
> > > > >
> > > > > thanks a lot for your efforts and support
> > > > >
> > > > > regarding queue, I mean percentage of queue from each stage: how many patients are waiting for Induction1, how many for Induction2, how many for Consolidation1 and consolidation2. All what I get is total number in queue.
> > > > >

> > > > > one more thing, is my model OK now or do you still see something that needs improvement?
> > > > >
> > > > >
> > > > > On Thursday, 9 June 2016, Iñaki Úcar <i.uc...@gmail.com> wrote:

> > > > > > What do you mean by "breakdown the queue"?

> > > > > > El 9/6/2016 8:55, "Mohamed Kamal" <mohamedk...@gmail.com> escribió:

> > > > > > > I also need to know if there is a way to breakdown the queue.

> > > > > > > thanks again in advance.
> > > > > > >
> > > > > > > On Thursday, 9 June 2016, Mohamed Kamal <mohamedk...@gmail.com> wrote:

> > > > > > > > please check the following modified script with branches, your feedback is highly appreciated...
> > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > library(simmer)
> > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > # rate of new patient arrival = 2.3 per week
> > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > # interarrival time (IAT)= 7/2.3 days
> > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > env <- simmer("AML-env")
> > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > ## add a new patient trajectory
> > > > > > > > newpatient <- create_trajectory("newAMLpatientpath") %>%
> > > > > > > >   branch(function() sample(c(1,2),size=1,replace=F,prob=c(0.999,0.001)), merge=c(T, T),
> > > > > > > >          create_trajectory("Induction1") %>%
> > > > > > > >            seize("bed", amount = 1, priority = 1) %>%
> > > > > > > >            seize("Induction1_in", amount = 1, priority = 1) %>%
> > > > > > > >            ## 31 day
> > > > > > > >            timeout(function() rnorm(1, 31, 2)) %>%
> > > > > > > >            release("bed", 1)%>%
> > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > >            #================ Induction 2
> > > > > > > >            branch(function() sample(c(1,2),size=1,replace=F,prob=c(0.842,0.158)), merge=c(T, T),
> > > > > > > >                   create_trajectory("Induction2") %>%
> > > > > > > >                     seize("bed", amount = 1, priority = 9) %>%
> > > > > > > >                     seize("Induction2_in", amount = 1, priority = 9) %>%
> > > > > > > >                     ## 28 day
> > > > > > > >                     timeout(function() rnorm(1, 28, 2)) %>%
> > > > > > > >                     release("bed", 1)%>%
> > > > > > > >                     #=============== Consolidation 1
> > > > > > > >                     branch(function() sample(c(1,2),size=1,replace=F,prob=c(0.746,0.254)), merge=c(T, T),
> > > > > > > >                            create_trajectory("Consolidation1") %>%
> > > > > > > >                              seize("bed", amount = 1, priority = 8) %>%
> > > > > > > >                              seize("Consolidation1_in", amount = 1, priority = 8) %>%
> > > > > > > >                              ## 25 day
> > > > > > > >                              timeout(function() rnorm(1, 25, 2)) %>%
> > > > > > > >                              release("bed", 1) %>%
> > > > > > > >                              #===============Consolidation 2
> > > > > > > >                              branch(function() sample(c(1,2),size=1,replace=F,prob=c(0.99,0.01)), merge=c(T, T),
> > > > > > > >                                     create_trajectory("Consolidation2") %>%
> > > > > > > >                                       seize("bed", amount = 1, priority = 8) %>%
> > > > > > > >                                       seize("Consolidation2_in", amount = 1, priority = 8) %>%
> > > > > > > >                                       ## 31.5 day
> > > > > > > >                                       timeout(function() rnorm(1, 31.5, 2)) %>%
> > > > > > > >                                       release("bed", 1)
> > > > > > > >                                     ,
> > > > > > > >                                     create_trajectory("Consolidation2_out") %>%
> > > > > > > >                                       seize("Consolidation2_out", amount = 1, priority = 1)
> > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > >                              )
> > > > > > > >                            #=============End Consolidation2
> > > > > > > >                            ,
> > > > > > > >                            create_trajectory("Consolidation1_out") %>%
> > > > > > > >                              seize("Consolidation1_out", amount = 1, priority = 1)
> > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > >                     )
> > > > > > > >                   #===============End Consolidation 1
> > > > > > > >                   ,
> > > > > > > >                   create_trajectory("Induction2_out") %>%
> > > > > > > >                     seize("Induction2_out", amount = 1, priority = 1)
> > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > >            )
> > > > > > > >          #=================End Induction 2
> > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > >          ,
> > > > > > > >          create_trajectory("Induction1_out") %>%
> > > > > > > >            seize("Induction1_out", amount = 1, priority = 1)
> > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > >   )
> > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > env %>%
> > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > >   ## add true resource
> > > > > > > >   add_resource("bed", 20) %>%
> > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > >   ## add resources for counting purpose
> > > > > > > >   add_resource("Induction1_in", Inf) %>%
> > > > > > > >   add_resource("Induction2_in", Inf) %>%
> > > > > > > >   add_resource("Consolidation1_in", Inf) %>%
> > > > > > > >   add_resource("Consolidation2_in", Inf) %>%
> > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > >   add_resource("Induction1_out", Inf) %>%
> > > > > > > >   add_resource("Induction2_out", Inf) %>%
> > > > > > > >   add_resource("Consolidation1_out", Inf) %>%
> > > > > > > >   add_resource("Consolidation2_out", Inf) %>%
> > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > >   add_generator("newpatient", newpatient, function() rnorm(1, mean=3.33, sd=0.5))
> > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > env %>% run(until=730) ## run for two years (365 * 2 = 730)
> > > > > > > > x<-env %>% get_mon_resources()
> > > > > > > > y<-env %>% get_mon_arrivals()
> > > > > > > > z<-env %>% get_mon_attributes()
> > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > plot_resource_utilization(env, c("bed"))
> > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > write.csv(y,"y.csv")
> > > > > > > > mean(x$queue)
> > > > > > > > arrivals <- get_mon_arrivals(env, per_resource = T)
> > > > > > > > write.csv(arrivals,"arrivals.csv")
> > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > On Wednesday, June 8, 2016 at 12:43:12 AM UTC+2, mokoka...@gmail.com wrote:
> > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > Dear Experts, need your opinion..
> > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > A center for treatment of leukemia has only 30 beds
> > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > Treatment involves the following process:
> > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > Induction 1--> Induction 2 --> Consolidation 1 --> Consolidation 2
> > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > Step #1 --> Induction 1
> > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > -accepting new cases to receive Chemotherapy Known as Induction 1 Regimen
> > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > -rate of arrival 2.3 patients / week
> > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > -average length of stay (ALOS) = 31 days
> > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > Step #2 -->  Induction 2
> > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > -84.2 % of patients from step #1 arrive successfully to this step
> > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > -ALOS = 28 days
> > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > -highest priority for admission
> > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > Step #3  --> Consolidation 1
> > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > -74.6% of patients from step#1 arrive successfully to this step
> > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > -ALOS = 25 days
> > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > - priority for admission less than step#2 but higher than step#1
> > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > Step #4 --> Consolidation 2
> > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > -73.5% of patients from step#1 arrive successfully to this step
> > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > -ALOS = 31.5 days
> > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > - priority for admission less than step#2 but higher than step#1
> > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > Using the R-script below, running the simulation for 2 years (730 days) and 30 beds gave the following
> > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > server status: 30(30) | queue status: 42
> > > > > > > > > > mean(x$queue)
> > > > > > > > > [1] 22.3562
> > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > Using the R-script below, running the simulation for 2 years (730 days) and 31 beds gave the following
> > > > > > > > > server status: 31(31) | queue status: 13
> > > > > > > > > > mean(x$queue)
> > > > > > > > > [1] 6.314767
> > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > Using the R-script below, running the simulation for 2 years (730 days) and 32 beds gave the following
> > > > > > > > > server status: 30(32) | queue status: 0
> > > > > > > > > > mean(x$queue)
> > > > > > > > > [1] 0.57
> > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > Does this mean that: "if I increase the center capacity from 30 to 32 beds, I will have no waiting list?"
> > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > ========================= R Script ==============================
> > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > library(simmer)
> > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > # rate of new patient arrival = 2.3 per week
> > > > > > > > > # inter-arrival time (IAT)= 7/2.3 days
> > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > #rn = interarrival time of new cases who will receive Induction 1
> > > > > > > > > rn <- 7/2.3 # IAT = 7/2.3, Priority = 1
> > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > #rind2 = interarrival time of patients who will receive Induction 2
> > > > > > > > > rind2 <- (1/0.842) * rn # priority = 9
> > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > #consol1 = interarrival time of patients who will receive consolidation 1
> > > > > > > > > rconsol1 <- (1/0.746) * rn # priority = 8
> > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > #consol1 = interarrival time of patients who will receive consolidation 2
> > > > > > > > > rconsol2 <- (1/0.735) * rn # priority = 8
> > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > env <- simmer("AML-env")
> > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > ## add a new patient trajectory
> > > > > > > > > newpatient <- create_trajectory("newAMLpatientpath") %>%
> > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > >   seize("bed", amount = 1, priority = 1) %>%
> > > > > > > > >   ## 31 day
> > > > > > > > >   timeout(function() rnorm(1, 31, 2)) %>%
> > > > > > > > >   release("bed", 1)
> > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > ## add a Induction2 patient trajectory
> > > > > > > > > rind2patient <- create_trajectory("rind2AMLpatientpath") %>%
> > > > > > > > >   seize("bed", amount = 1, priority = 9) %>%
> > > > > > > > >   ## 28 days
> > > > > > > > >   timeout(function() rnorm(1, 28, 2)) %>%
> > > > > > > > >   release("bed", 1)
> > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > ## add a Consolidation1 patient trajectory
> > > > > > > > > consol1patient <- create_trajectory("consol1AMLpatientpath") %>%
> > > > > > > > >     seize("bed", amount = 1, priority = 8) %>%
> > > > > > > > >   ## 25 days
> > > > > > > > >   timeout(function() rnorm(1, 25, 2)) %>%
> > > > > > > > >   release("bed", 1)
> > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > ## add a Consolidation2 patient trajectory
> > > > > > > > > consol2patient <- create_trajectory("consol2AMLpatientpath") %>%
> > > > > > > > >     seize("bed", amount = 1, priority = 8) %>%
> > > > > > > > >   ## 31.5 days
> > > > > > > > >   timeout(function() rnorm(1, 31.5, 2)) %>%
> > > > > > > > >   release("bed", 1)
> > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > env %>%
> > > > > > > > >   add_resource("bed", 30) %>%
> > > > > > > > >   add_generator("newpatient", newpatient, function() rn) %>%
> > > > > > > > >   add_generator("rind2patient", rind2patient, function() rind2) %>%
> > > > > > > > >   add_generator("consol1patient", consol1patient, function() rconsol1) %>%
> > > > > > > > >   add_generator("consol2patient", consol2patient, function() rconsol2)
> > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > env %>% run(until=730) ## run for two years (365 * 2 = 730)
> > > > > > > > > x<-env %>% get_mon_resources()
> > > > > > > > > y<-env %>% get_mon_arrivals()
> > > > > > > > > mean(x$queue)

On Fri, Jun 10, 2016 at 7:08 AM, Mohamed Kamal <mohamedk...@gmail.com> wrote:
| So, do you think this model is OK ? I mean, if the percentages are matching reality, shall i depend on it to predict scenarios?

What do you mean matching reality? Model validation is important. Did you do a statistical prop test or ANOVA? If so, what were the results, etc? How much data do you have from reality?

Then if the model is validated for known parameters, to change those to areas outside observed usually results in extrapolation. It's important to be aware of the dangers of extrapolation. The changes made, may change external behaviors, or there may be factors that come into play that weren't part of the original model. With this cautionary note, it's still a powerful technique. Make sure that the final statistical method used is for computing predicted intervals and not confidence intervals.

---

Shawn Garbett
Vanderbilt Biostatistics

To avoid a branch inside a branch inside a branch… I would simulate something like this:
patient <- create_trajectory() %>%
  seize("waiting_induction1", 1) %>%
  seize("bed", 1, priority=induction1) %>%
  release("waiting_induction1", 1) %>%
  timeout(induction1_timeout) %>%
  branch(induction1_prob_continue, c(T, F),
         create_trajectory() %>% release("bed"),
         create_trajectory() %>% release("bed")) %>%
  seize("waiting_induction2", 1) %>%
  seize("bed", 1, priority=induction2) %>%
  release("waiting_induction2", 1) %>%
  timeout(induction2_timeout) %>%
  ...

and so on, where “waiting_induction1”, “waiting_induction2”… are resources with infinite capacity allocated to count how many patients are waiting for each stage.

messages.body_plain:
Brute force using a global (there's certainly a better way):

tenatatime_cnt <- 0
tenatatime <- function()
{
  if(tenatatime_cnt == 0)
  {
    tenatatime_cnt <<- 9
    rexp(1)
  }
  else
  {
    tenatatime_cnt <<- tenatatime_cnt - 1
    0
  }
}

env %>% add_generator("patient", traj, tenatatime)

Note this goes on forever now.

messages.subject: New feature: strict queue size
messages.subject_clean: New feature: strict queue size
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

New option queue_size_strict for add_resource. By default, the behaviour does not change. But queue_size_strict=TRUE guarantees that queue_size is not exceeded with preemption enabled (see #59 <https://github.com/r-simmer/simmer/issues/59>).

Regards,
​
--
Iñaki Úcar

@Enchufa2 <https://twitter.com/#%21/Enchufa2>

messages.subject: Modeling tank inventory
messages.subject_clean: Modeling tank inventory
messages.body_plain:
I am hoping someone can give me some guidance on how to use simmer to model the following situation:

Ships arriving randomly to a dock where the product is loaded into a refinery tank. The loaded product is then consumed at the refinery at a given rate.  The refinery tank has finite inventory (non-zero queue).  The complication arises that if the refinery tank is full, product should not be loaded in the dock until inventory space becomes available.  I have tried to use set attribute and conditional logic to identify the situation when the tank is full to prevent the ship from being loaded into the refinery tank.  The dock resource will have infinite queue as I am trying to determine the optimum refinery tank capacity to minimize wait time. However, with my logic the arrival is being rejected.  Any suggestions on how to model this scenario with simmer would be appreciated.

My code is provided below.

Thanks,
Jose

library(simmer)

library(ggplot2)

library(plyr)

library(dplyr)

library(parallel)

library(doBy)

library(xlsx)

set.seed(1234)

#time increment is 1 days and volume increment 500Mbbls

lambda1 <- 1/(500/122.2)  #average one 500 Mbbl ship every 4.09 days or 100Mbbls per day

lambda2 <- 1/(500/80)  #average one 500 Mbbl ship every 6.25 days  or

lambda3 <- 0.001  #average one 500 Mbbl ship every 8 days or 100Mbbls per day

lambda4 <- 0.001  #average one 500 Mbbl ship every 7 days  or

lambda1 <- 1/(500/110)  #average one 500 Mbbl ship every 4.54 days or 100Mbbls per day

lambda2 <- 1/(500/165.9)  #average one 500 Mbbl ship every 3.0 days  or

lambda3 <- 0.001  #average one 500 Mbbl ship every 3.6 days or 100Mbbls per day

lambda4 <- 0.001  #NA

env<-simmer()

simulation<- function(t) {

    t1<-create_trajectory() %>%

    set_attribute("available1", function() {

     if (env %>%  get_queue_count("Term2")<2) 1

      else 0 }) %>%

    seize("Term1", amount=function(attrs) {

      if (attrs["available1"] == 1 &&

          env %>% get_server_count("Term1")==0) 1    # serve

      else 0                                     # no serve

    }) %>%

    timeout(function(attrs) {

      if (attrs["available1"] == 1 &&

          env %>% get_server_count("Term1")==0) 26.5/24    # serve

      else 2                                     # no serve

    }) %>%

    release("Term1", function(attrs)attrs[["available1"]])%>%

    seize("Term2", amount=1) %>%

    timeout(function() 500/122.2) %>%

   # timeout(function() 500/110) %>%

    release("Term2", amount=1)

    t2<-create_trajectory() %>%

    set_attribute("available2", function() {

     if (env %>%  get_queue_count("Term3")<1) 1

      else 0 }) %>%

    seize("Term1", amount=function(attrs) {

      if (attrs["available2"] == 1 &&

          env %>% get_server_count("Term1")==0) 1    # serve

      else 2                                     # no serve

    }) %>%

 timeout(function(attrs) {

      if (attrs["available2"] == 1 &&

          env %>% get_server_count("Term1")==0) 26.5/24    # serve

      else 2                                     # no serve

    }) %>%

   # timeout(function() 26.5/24) %>%

    release("Term1", function(attrs)attrs[["available2"]])%>%

    seize("Term3", amount=1) %>%

     timeout(function() 500/80) %>%

   # timeout(function() 500/165.9) %>%

    release("Term3", amount=1)

    t3<-create_trajectory() %>%

    seize("Term1", amount=1) %>%

    timeout(function() 1) %>%

    release("Term1", amount=1)

    t4<-create_trajectory() %>%

    seize("Term1", amount=1) %>%

    timeout(function() 1) %>%

    release("Term1", amount=1)

  env<-simmer() %>%

    add_resource("Term1", capacity=1, queue_size=Inf,preemptive=TRUE,preempt_order="fifo") %>%

   add_resource("Term2", capacity=1, queue_size=2,preemptive=TRUE,preempt_order="fifo") %>%

   add_resource("Term3", capacity=1, queue_size=1,preemptive=TRUE,preempt_order="fifo") %>%

   add_generator("acid", t1, from_to(0, 365, function() runif(1, 4, 5))) %>%

   add_generator("hvysour", t2, from_to(0, 365, function() runif(1, 3, 5))) %>%

    add_generator("canhvy", t3, function() rexp(1, lambda3)) %>%

    add_generator("light", t4, function() rexp(1, lambda4))

     env %>% run(until=t)

}

time<-365

env<-simulation(time)

get_mon_arrivals(env)

messages.subject: Re: [simmer-devel] Modeling tank inventory
messages.subject_clean: [simmer-devel] Modeling tank inventory
messages.body_plain:
Hi Jose, welcome to the list.

I don't know if I understand the problem. I cannot identify which parts of your model correspond to which elements of the problem description. What are the "terms"? Why does one of them have an infinite queue while the others have finite ones (that's why you have rejections, by the way)? What's the meaning of each trajectory?

What I understand from your description is that you have a producer-consumer problem. This can be modelled more naturally with a resource like a container or a storage supporting put/get methods. This kind of resources are not implemented in simmer yet, but they're in our schedule. Meanwhile, since simmer's resource is pretty flexible, you can mimic the put/get behaviour thanks to the independence of seize/release.

Therefore, from your description, I would expect one trajectory per producer, which only seizes (puts stuff into) the resource, and one trajectory per consumer, which only releases (gets stuff from) the resource. However, all your trajectories perform seizes and releases, which seems confusing to me.

Also I would suggest you refine your optimisation objective. Because if you only want to minimise the waiting time, the response is immediate: an infinite capacity minimises the waiting time. So I suspect that you have more restrictions to apply.

Regards,
Iñaki

Here is updated code renaming term 1 to Dock.  So I have ships for two types of crudes arriving at a dock.  I show four in my code but for now I am focusing only on two of the crudes. Both crude types use the same dock but only one ship at a time.  The dock has infinite queue as I am trying to compute the time that the ships wait at the dock to compute demurrage costs. The catch is that ships can only use the dock if space is available in their corresponding downstream tanks (Term 2 and Term3).  The problem is that if a ships discharges at the dock and no space is available in the tank (limited queue 2 for Term 2 and 1 for Term3), I do not want the ship to be rejected but should not be allowed to discharge at the dock unless there is space in the downstream tank). I am new to simmer as you can probably tell.  Can I use branch or rollback or a combination of them to model this situation.  Very much appreciate your help.

Thanks,

Jose

library(simmer)
library(ggplot2)
library(plyr)
library(dplyr)
library(parallel)
library(doBy)
library(xlsx)

set.seed(1234)

#time increment is 1 days and volume increment 500Mbbls
lambda1 <- 1/(500/122.2)  #average one 500 Mbbl ship every 4.09 days or 100Mbbls per day
lambda2 <- 1/(500/80)  #average one 500 Mbbl ship every 6.25 days  or
lambda3 <- 0.001  #average one 500 Mbbl ship every 8 days or 100Mbbls per day
lambda4 <- 0.001  #average one 500 Mbbl ship every 7 days  or
lambda1 <- 1/(500/110)  #average one 500 Mbbl ship every 4.54 days or 100Mbbls per day
lambda2 <- 1/(500/165.9)  #average one 500 Mbbl ship every 3.0 days  or
lambda3 <- 0.001  #average one 500 Mbbl ship every 3.6 days or 100Mbbls per day
lambda4 <- 0.001  #NA
env<-simmer()
simulation<- function(t) {
    t1<-create_trajectory() %>%

    set_attribute("available1", function() {
     if (env %>%  get_queue_count("Term2")<2) 1
      else 0 }) %>%

    seize("Dock", amount=function(attrs) {

      if (attrs["available1"] == 1 &&

          env %>% get_server_count("Dock")==0) 1    # serve

      else 0                                     # no serve
    }) %>%

    timeout(function(attrs) {
      if (attrs["available1"] == 1 &&

          env %>% get_server_count("Dock")==0) 26.5/24    # serve

      else 2                                     # no serve
    }) %>%

    release("Dock", function(attrs)attrs[["available1"]])%>%

    seize("Term2", amount=1) %>%
    timeout(function() 500/122.2) %>%
   # timeout(function() 500/110) %>%
    release("Term2", amount=1)

    t2<-create_trajectory() %>%
    set_attribute("available2", function() {
     if (env %>%  get_queue_count("Term3")<1) 1
      else 0 }) %>%

    seize("Dock", amount=function(attrs) {

      if (attrs["available2"] == 1 &&

          env %>% get_server_count("Dock")==0) 1    # serve

      else 2                                     # no serve
    }) %>%

 timeout(function(attrs) {
      if (attrs["available2"] == 1 &&

          env %>% get_server_count("Dock")==0) 26.5/24    # serve

      else 2                                     # no serve
    }) %>%

   # timeout(function() 26.5/24) %>%

    release("Dock", function(attrs)attrs[["available2"]])%>%

    seize("Term3", amount=1) %>%
     timeout(function() 500/80) %>%
   # timeout(function() 500/165.9) %>%
    release("Term3", amount=1)

    t3<-create_trajectory() %>%
    seize("Dock", amount=1) %>%
    timeout(function() 1) %>%
    release("Dock", amount=1)

    t4<-create_trajectory() %>%
    seize("Dock", amount=1) %>%
    timeout(function() 1) %>%
    release("Dock", amount=1)

  env<-simmer() %>%
    add_resource("Dock", capacity=1, queue_size=Inf,preemptive=TRUE,preempt_order="fifo") %>%

   add_resource("Term2", capacity=1, queue_size=2,preemptive=TRUE,preempt_order="fifo") %>%
   add_resource("Term3", capacity=1, queue_size=1,preemptive=TRUE,preempt_order="fifo") %>%
   add_generator("acid", t1, from_to(0, 365, function() runif(1, 4, 5))) %>%
   add_generator("hvysour", t2, from_to(0, 365, function() runif(1, 3, 5))) %>%
    add_generator("canhvy", t3, function() rexp(1, lambda3)) %>%
    add_generator("light", t4, function() rexp(1, lambda4))
     env %>% run(until=t)
}

env<-simulation(time)
get_mon_arrivals(env)

messages.body_plain:
So you don't need attributes at all, and all your resources must have infinite queues:
A ship tries to seize the dock (a seize blocks while the arrival stays in the queue).
When the ship gains the dock, it tries to seize the corresponding tank. So if the resource's server (the tank) is full, it waits in the resource's infinite queue (waits in the dock).
When the latter seize unblocks, it means that the cargo is finally in the tank, so the ship leaves.
And of course, you'll need another trajectory for releasing the tanks.

messages.body_plain:
Is there a good example out there? The tanks have finite inventory and I need to evaluate the impact of increasing tank inventory on ship demur rage. There is an extra fee for ship wait time. To make sure we are on the same page, one dock common  to both crude types and each crude type different tank and different withdrawal rate for each tank. Each crude type has its own trajectory but both start at the same dock. Refinery tanks have finite inventory capacity but the dock itself has infinite queue as they are waiting on the water.

Thanks again,

Jose

Sent from my iPhone

On Jun 24, 2016, at 11:28 AM, Iñaki Úcar <i.uc...@gmail.com> wrote:

> So you don't need attributes at all, and all your resources must have infinite queues:
> A ship tries to seize the dock (a seize blocks while the arrival stays in the queue).
> When the ship gains the dock, it tries to seize the corresponding tank. So if the resource's server (the tank) is full, it waits in the resource's infinite queue (waits in the dock).
> When the latter seize unblocks, it means that the cargo is finally in the tank, so the ship leaves.
> And of course, you'll need another trajectory for releasing the tanks.

The point is ship can not seize dock until space in the tank downstream.

Thanks again,

Jose

Sent from my iPhone

On Jun 24, 2016, at 11:28 AM, Iñaki Úcar <i.uc...@gmail.com> wrote:

> So you don't need attributes at all, and all your resources must have infinite queues:
> A ship tries to seize the dock (a seize blocks while the arrival stays in the queue).
> When the ship gains the dock, it tries to seize the corresponding tank. So if the resource's server (the tank) is full, it waits in the resource's infinite queue (waits in the dock).
> When the latter seize unblocks, it means that the cargo is finally in the tank, so the ship leaves.
> And of course, you'll need another trajectory for releasing the tanks.
>

The catch is that ships can only use the dock if space is available in their corresponding downstream tanks (Term 2 and Term3).  The problem is that if a ships discharges at the dock and no space is available in the tank (limited queue 2 for Term 2 and 1 for Term3), I do not want the ship to be rejected but should not be allowed to discharge at the dock unless there is space in the downstream tank). messages.body_plain:
Ok. Then you can use two helper resources with capacity=1 before the dock, one for each type of cargo. As soon as one tank gets full, you can set capacity=0 for the corresponding helper resource, and the ships containing that kind of cargo cannot access the dock. The capacity becomes 1 again when there is room in the tank, so the first ship in the queue seizes the dock.

2016-06-24 19:31 GMT+02:00 Jose Bird <jose...@gmail.com>:

>
> Thanks again!
>
> Jose
>
> Sent from my iPhone

> On Jun 24, 2016, at 12:23 PM, Iñaki Úcar <i.uc...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> > Ok. Then you can use two helper resources with capacity=1 before the dock, one for each type of cargo. As soon as one tank gets full, you can set capacity=0 for the corresponding helper resource, and the ships containing that kind of cargo cannot access the dock. The capacity becomes 1 again when there is room in the tank, so the first ship in the queue seizes the dock.
> >

> > > The point is ship can not seize dock until space in the tank downstream.
> > >
> > > Thanks again,
> > >
> > > Jose

> > > On Jun 24, 2016, at 11:28 AM, Iñaki Úcar <i.uc...@gmail.com> wrote:
> > >
> > > > So you don't need attributes at all, and all your resources must have infinite queues:
> > > > A ship tries to seize the dock (a seize blocks while the arrival stays in the queue).
> > > > When the ship gains the dock, it tries to seize the corresponding tank. So if the resource's server (the tank) is full, it waits in the resource's infinite queue (waits in the dock).
> > > > When the latter seize unblocks, it means that the cargo is finally in the tank, so the ship leaves.
> > > > And of course, you'll need another trajectory for releasing the tanks.
> > > >
> > > > 2016-06-24 17:36 GMT+02:00 Jose Bird <jose...@gmail.com>:

> > > > > Thank you so much for the quick response, Inaki!!
> > > > >
> > > > > Here is updated code renaming term 1 to Dock.  So I have ships for two types of crudes arriving at a dock.  I show four in my code but for now I am focusing only on two of the crudes. Both crude types use the same dock but only one ship at a time.  The dock has infinite queue as I am trying to compute the time that the ships wait at the dock to compute demurrage costs. The catch is that ships can only use the dock if space is available in their corresponding downstream tanks (Term 2 and Term3).  The problem is that if a ships discharges at the dock and no space is available in the tank (limited queue 2 for Term 2 and 1 for Term3), I do not want the ship to be rejected but should not be allowed to discharge at the dock unless there is space in the downstream tank). I am new to simmer as you can probably tell.  Can I use branch or rollback or a combination of them to model this situation.  Very much appreciate your help.

> > > > > > Ships arriving randomly to a dock where the product is loaded into a refinery tank. The loaded product is then consumed at the refinery at a given rate. I have tried to use set attribute and conditional logic to identify the situation when the tank is full to prevent the ship from being loaded into the refinery tank.  The dock resource will have infinite queue as I am trying to determine the optimum refinery tank capacity to minimize wait time. However, with my logic the arrival is being rejected.  Any suggestions on how to model this scenario with simmer would be appreciated.

messages.body_plain:
Mmmh... forget my previous idea. Better than changing the capacity, you can do this:
seize the helper resource for this kind of cargo.
seize the dock.
branch
if there is room in the tank, unload and leave.
if not, release the dock and rollback to 2.
And note that your "refine tank inventory" is the resource's capacity, not the queue size. The queue size must be zero.

> seize the dock.
> branch

messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

There was critical mass enough to release another version of simmer, and the last bug, reported in #67 <https://github.com/r-simmer/simmer/issues/67>, was the final trigger. Therefore, simmer 3.3.0 was released and it's already on CRAN. Windows users will need to wait until the CRAN backend builds the binaries for your platform.

Regards,
--

messages.body_plain:
OK, I see. But I think that leave() cannot be used if I want the two branches to seize the resources at different priorities and timeouts for example ..

 branch(function() sample(c(1,2),size=1,replace=T,prob=c(0.2,0.8)), merge=c(T, T),
                                            create_trajectory("relapse") %>%
                                            seize("bed", amount = 1, priority = 1) %>%
                                            seize("relapse", amount = 1, priority = 1) %>%
                                            timeout(function() rnorm(1, 40, 2)) %>%
                                            release("bed", 1)
                                               ,

                                             create_trajectory("relapse_out") %>%
                                             seize("bed", amount = 1, priority = 9) %>%
                                             seize("relapse_out", amount = 1, priority = 1)  %>%
                                             timeout(function() rnorm(1, 10, 2)) %>%
                                             release("bed", 1)

                                      )

So, in such case there is no other option but to use branch inside a branch, right?
