messages.body_plain:
I was talking about the points in your trajectory, at the end of each stage, where a patient may leave with some probability. The case you mention is different, of course.

2016-06-28 21:33 GMT+02:00 moko kamello <mokoka...@gmail.com>:

> OK, I see. But I think that leave() cannot be used if I want the two branches to seize the resources at different priorities and timeouts for example ..
>
>  branch(function() sample(c(1,2),size=1,replace=T,prob=c(0.2,0.8)), merge=c(T, T),
>                                             create_trajectory("relapse") %>%
>                                             seize("bed", amount = 1, priority = 1) %>%
>                                             seize("relapse", amount = 1, priority = 1) %>%
>                                             timeout(function() rnorm(1, 40, 2)) %>%
>                                             release("bed", 1)
>                                                ,
>
>                                              create_trajectory("relapse_out") %>%
>                                              seize("bed", amount = 1, priority = 9) %>%
>                                              seize("relapse_out", amount = 1, priority = 1)  %>%
>                                              timeout(function() rnorm(1, 10, 2)) %>%
>                                              release("bed", 1)
>
>                                       )
>
> So, in such case there is no other option but to use branch inside a branch, right?
>
> On 28 June 2016 at 11:26, Iñaki Úcar <i.uc...@gmail.com> wrote:
> > See the associated issue: https://github.com/r-simmer/simmer/issues/63
> >
> > 2016-06-28 11:24 GMT+02:00 moko kamello <mokoka...@gmail.com>:
> > >
> > > Have any sample ?
> > > On Jun 28, 2016 11:19 AM, "Iñaki Úcar" <i.uc...@gmail.com> wrote:
> > > >
> > > > BTW, in order to avoid so many nested branches in your model, you’ll be probably interested in the new activity called leave, which does exactly what you need: leave a trajectory with some probability.
> > > > ​
> > > >
> > > > 2016-06-27 19:53 GMT+02:00 Iñaki Úcar <i.uc...@gmail.com>:
> > > > > The bug is already fixed. Check out the master branch on GitHub. The CRAN version has the bug and does NOT work properly.
> > > > >
> > > > > 2016-06-27 18:55 GMT+02:00 moko kamello <mokoka...@gmail.com>:
> > > > > >
> > > > > > For a reason or another the only version working is the one on CRAN. Is there any snippet of script to prevent cumulative sum of timeout inside a branch
> > > > > > On Jun 27, 2016 4:10 AM, "moko kamello" <mokoka...@gmail.com> wrote:
> > > > > > > Attached simpler example with cummulative time calculated for a branch
> > > > > > >
> > > > > > > On 27 June 2016 at 03:45, moko kamello <mokoka...@gmail.com> wrote:
> > > > > > > > Now, using the latest CRAN version, I think the error results from the cumulative sum of time within each branch, this will result in activity time to become greater and lead to -ve values. Just an opinion.
> > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > On 26 June 2016 at 22:58, Iñaki Úcar <i.uc...@gmail.com> wrote:
> > > > > > > > > Use the version 3.1.2.
> > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > 2016-06-26 22:54 GMT+02:00 moko kamello <mokoka...@gmail.com>:
> > > > > > > > > > Is there any quick work around until this issue is resolved ?
> > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > > On 26 June 2016 at 10:00, Iñaki Úcar <i.uc...@gmail.com> wrote:
> > > > > > > > > > > I've opened an issue <https://github.com/r-simmer/simmer/issues/67> on GitHub. If anyone finds a smaller piece of code featuring this bug, please, post it there.
> > > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > > > 2016-06-26 9:42 GMT+02:00 moko kamello <mokoka...@gmail.com>:
> > > > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > > > > Thanks
> > > > > > > > > > > > On Jun 26, 2016 9:39 AM, "Iñaki Úcar" <i.uc...@gmail.com> wrote:
> > > > > > > > > > > > > You can download every release from the Releases page: https://github.com/r-simmer/simmer/releases
> > > > > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > > > > > 2016-06-26 9:33 GMT+02:00 moko kamello <mokoka...@gmail.com>:
> > > > > > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > > > > > > Could you please send me a zip file to install it as I have no experience to install it from github
> > > > > > > > > > > > > > On Jun 26, 2016 9:28 AM, "Iñaki Úcar" <i.uc...@gmail.com> wrote:
> > > > > > > > > > > > > > > Actually the current CRAN version (3.2.1) does NOT give correct results either, sorry. It's the release 3.1.2 which gives the correct results.
> > > > > > > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > > > > > > > 2016-06-26 9:12 GMT+02:00 Iñaki Úcar <i.uc...@gmail.com>:
> > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > It seems there's a bug in the development version. The version on CRAN gives correct results though. It would be great if you could reproduce this problem with a much simpler example. It would help me debug the issue.
> > > > > > > > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > 2016-06-26 6:53 GMT+02:00 moko kamello <mokoka...@gmail.com>:
> > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > I don't know if this is my bad: the waiting time is positive only if in case of get_mon_arrival(env, per_resources=F)
> > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > However, It gives me mixed positive and negative values in case of per_resource=T and I have absolutely no clue why this happens
> > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > Any Help ?
> > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > On 20 June 2016 at 10:34, Iñaki Úcar <i.uc...@gmail.com> wrote:
> > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > 2016-06-18 1:05 GMT+02:00 moko kamello <mokoka...@gmail.com>:
> > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > Is it possible that "waiting time" be negative values ?
> > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > No, it's not.

messages.body_plain:
Congratulations for version 3.3 btw

On Jun 29, 2016 2:01 PM, "Iñaki Úcar" <i.uc...@gmail.com> wrote:

> I was talking about the points in your trajectory, at the end of each stage, where a patient may leave with some probability. The case you mention is different, of course.
>
> 2016-06-28 21:33 GMT+02:00 moko kamello <mokoka...@gmail.com>:
> > OK, I see. But I think that leave() cannot be used if I want the two branches to seize the resources at different priorities and timeouts for example ..
> >
> >  branch(function() sample(c(1,2),size=1,replace=T,prob=c(0.2,0.8)), merge=c(T, T),
> >                                             create_trajectory("relapse") %>%
> >                                             seize("bed", amount = 1, priority = 1) %>%
> >                                             seize("relapse", amount = 1, priority = 1) %>%
> >                                             timeout(function() rnorm(1, 40, 2)) %>%
> >                                             release("bed", 1)
> >                                                ,
> >
> >                                              create_trajectory("relapse_out") %>%
> >                                              seize("bed", amount = 1, priority = 9) %>%
> >                                              seize("relapse_out", amount = 1, priority = 1)  %>%
> >                                              timeout(function() rnorm(1, 10, 2)) %>%
> >                                              release("bed", 1)
> >
> >                                       )
> >
> > So, in such case there is no other option but to use branch inside a branch, right?
> >
> > On 28 June 2016 at 11:26, Iñaki Úcar <i.uc...@gmail.com> wrote:
> > > See the associated issue: https://github.com/r-simmer/simmer/issues/63
> > >
> > > 2016-06-28 11:24 GMT+02:00 moko kamello <mokoka...@gmail.com>:
> > > >
> > > > Have any sample ?
> > > > On Jun 28, 2016 11:19 AM, "Iñaki Úcar" <i.uc...@gmail.com> wrote:
> > > > >
> > > > > BTW, in order to avoid so many nested branches in your model, you’ll be probably interested in the new activity called leave, which does exactly what you need: leave a trajectory with some probability.
> > > > > ​
> > > > >
> > > > > 2016-06-27 19:53 GMT+02:00 Iñaki Úcar <i.uc...@gmail.com>:
> > > > > > The bug is already fixed. Check out the master branch on GitHub. The CRAN version has the bug and does NOT work properly.
> > > > > >
> > > > > > 2016-06-27 18:55 GMT+02:00 moko kamello <mokoka...@gmail.com>:
> > > > > > >
> > > > > > > For a reason or another the only version working is the one on CRAN. Is there any snippet of script to prevent cumulative sum of timeout inside a branch
> > > > > > > On Jun 27, 2016 4:10 AM, "moko kamello" <mokoka...@gmail.com> wrote:
> > > > > > > > Attached simpler example with cummulative time calculated for a branch
> > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > On 27 June 2016 at 03:45, moko kamello <mokoka...@gmail.com> wrote:
> > > > > > > > > Now, using the latest CRAN version, I think the error results from the cumulative sum of time within each branch, this will result in activity time to become greater and lead to -ve values. Just an opinion.
> > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > On 26 June 2016 at 22:58, Iñaki Úcar <i.uc...@gmail.com> wrote:
> > > > > > > > > > Use the version 3.1.2.
> > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > > 2016-06-26 22:54 GMT+02:00 moko kamello <mokoka...@gmail.com>:
> > > > > > > > > > > Is there any quick work around until this issue is resolved ?
> > > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > > > On 26 June 2016 at 10:00, Iñaki Úcar <i.uc...@gmail.com> wrote:
> > > > > > > > > > > > I've opened an issue <https://github.com/r-simmer/simmer/issues/67> on GitHub. If anyone finds a smaller piece of code featuring this bug, please, post it there.
> > > > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > > > > 2016-06-26 9:42 GMT+02:00 moko kamello <mokoka...@gmail.com>:
> > > > > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > > > > > Thanks
> > > > > > > > > > > > > On Jun 26, 2016 9:39 AM, "Iñaki Úcar" <i.uc...@gmail.com> wrote:
> > > > > > > > > > > > > > You can download every release from the Releases page: https://github.com/r-simmer/simmer/releases
> > > > > > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > > > > > > 2016-06-26 9:33 GMT+02:00 moko kamello <mokoka...@gmail.com>:
> > > > > > > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > > > > > > > Could you please send me a zip file to install it as I have no experience to install it from github
> > > > > > > > > > > > > > > On Jun 26, 2016 9:28 AM, "Iñaki Úcar" <i.uc...@gmail.com> wrote:
> > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > Actually the current CRAN version (3.2.1) does NOT give correct results either, sorry. It's the release 3.1.2 which gives the correct results.
> > > > > > > > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > 2016-06-26 9:12 GMT+02:00 Iñaki Úcar <i.uc...@gmail.com>:
> > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > It seems there's a bug in the development version. The version on CRAN gives correct results though. It would be great if you could reproduce this problem with a much simpler example. It would help me debug the issue.
> > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > 2016-06-26 6:53 GMT+02:00 moko kamello <mokoka...@gmail.com>:
> > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > I don't know if this is my bad: the waiting time is positive only if in case of get_mon_arrival(env, per_resources=F)
> > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > However, It gives me mixed positive and negative values in case of per_resource=T and I have absolutely no clue why this happens
> > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > Any Help ?
> > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > On 20 June 2016 at 10:34, Iñaki Úcar <i.uc...@gmail.com> wrote:
> > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > 2016-06-18 1:05 GMT+02:00 moko kamello <mokoka...@gmail.com>:
> > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > Is it possible that "waiting time" be negative values ?
> > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > No, it's not.
> > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > Iñaki

messages.body_plain:
in get_mon_resources(env, per_resource=T) i see only finished=TRUE. Is
there a way to get the finished=FALSE?

On 29 June 2016 at 14:08, moko kamello <mokoka...@gmail.com> wrote:
> Congratulations for version 3.3 btw
>
> On Jun 29, 2016 2:01 PM, "Iñaki Úcar" <i.uc...@gmail.com> wrote:
>>
>> I was talking about the points in your trajectory, at the end of each
>> stage, where a patient may leave with some probability. The case you mention
>> is different, of course.
>>
>> 2016-06-28 21:33 GMT+02:00 moko kamello <mokoka...@gmail.com>:
>>>
>>> OK, I see. But I think that leave() cannot be used if I want the two
>>> branches to seize the resources at different priorities and timeouts for
>>> example ..
>>>
>>>  branch(function() sample(c(1,2),size=1,replace=T,prob=c(0.2,0.8)),
>>> merge=c(T, T),
>>>                                             create_trajectory("relapse")
>>> %>%
>>>                                             seize("bed", amount = 1,
>>> priority = 1) %>%
>>>                                             seize("relapse", amount = 1,
>>> priority = 1) %>%
>>>                                             timeout(function() rnorm(1,
>>> 40, 2)) %>%
>>>                                             release("bed", 1)
>>>                                                ,
>>>
>>>
>>> create_trajectory("relapse_out") %>%
>>>                                              seize("bed", amount = 1,
>>> priority = 9) %>%
>>>                                              seize("relapse_out", amount
>>> = 1, priority = 1)  %>%
>>>                                              timeout(function() rnorm(1,
>>> 10, 2)) %>%
>>>                                              release("bed", 1)
>>>
>>>                                       )
>>>
>>> So, in such case there is no other option but to use branch inside a
>>> branch, right?
>>>
>>>
>>> On 28 June 2016 at 11:26, Iñaki Úcar <i.uc...@gmail.com> wrote:
>>>>
>>>> See the associated issue: https://github.com/r-simmer/simmer/issues/63
>>>>
>>>> 2016-06-28 11:24 GMT+02:00 moko kamello <mokoka...@gmail.com>:
>>>>>
>>>>> Have any sample ?
>>>>>
>>>>> On Jun 28, 2016 11:19 AM, "Iñaki Úcar" <i.uc...@gmail.com> wrote:
>>>>>>
>>>>>> BTW, in order to avoid so many nested branches in your model, you’ll
>>>>>> be probably interested in the new activity called leave, which does exactly
>>>>>> what you need: leave a trajectory with some probability.
>>>>>>
>>>>>>
>>>>>> 2016-06-27 19:53 GMT+02:00 Iñaki Úcar <i.uc...@gmail.com>:
>>>>>>>
>>>>>>> The bug is already fixed. Check out the master branch on GitHub. The
>>>>>>> CRAN version has the bug and does NOT work properly.
>>>>>>>
>>>>>>> 2016-06-27 18:55 GMT+02:00 moko kamello <mokoka...@gmail.com>:
>>>>>>>>
>>>>>>>> For a reason or another the only version working is the one on CRAN.
>>>>>>>> Is there any snippet of script to prevent cumulative sum of timeout inside a
>>>>>>>> branch
>>>>>>>>
>>>>>>>> On Jun 27, 2016 4:10 AM, "moko kamello" <mokoka...@gmail.com>
>>>>>>>> wrote:
>>>>>>>>>
>>>>>>>>> Attached simpler example with cummulative time calculated for a
>>>>>>>>> branch
>>>>>>>>>
>>>>>>>>> On 27 June 2016 at 03:45, moko kamello <mokoka...@gmail.com>
>>>>>>>>> wrote:
>>>>>>>>>>
>>>>>>>>>> Now, using the latest CRAN version, I think the error results from
>>>>>>>>>> the cumulative sum of time within each branch, this will result in activity
>>>>>>>>>> time to become greater and lead to -ve values. Just an opinion.
>>>>>>>>>>
>>>>>>>>>> On 26 June 2016 at 22:58, Iñaki Úcar <i.uc...@gmail.com> wrote:
>>>>>>>>>>>
>>>>>>>>>>> Use the version 3.1.2.
>>>>>>>>>>>
>>>>>>>>>>> 2016-06-26 22:54 GMT+02:00 moko kamello <mokoka...@gmail.com>:
>>>>>>>>>>>>
>>>>>>>>>>>> Is there any quick work around until this issue is resolved ?
>>>>>>>>>>>>
>>>>>>>>>>>> On 26 June 2016 at 10:00, Iñaki Úcar <i.uc...@gmail.com> wrote:
>>>>>>>>>>>>>
>>>>>>>>>>>>> I've opened an issue on GitHub. If anyone finds a smaller piece
>>>>>>>>>>>>> of code featuring this bug, please, post it there.
>>>>>>>>>>>>>
>>>>>>>>>>>>> 2016-06-26 9:42 GMT+02:00 moko kamello
>>>>>>>>>>>>> <mokoka...@gmail.com>:
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>
>>>>>>>>>>>>>> Thanks
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>
>>>>>>>>>>>>>> On Jun 26, 2016 9:39 AM, "Iñaki Úcar" <i.uc...@gmail.com>
>>>>>>>>>>>>>> wrote:
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> You can download every release from the Releases page:
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> https://github.com/r-simmer/simmer/releases
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> 2016-06-26 9:33 GMT+02:00 moko kamello
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> <mokoka...@gmail.com>:
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> Could you please send me a zip file to install it as I have
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> no experience to install it from github
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> On Jun 26, 2016 9:28 AM, "Iñaki Úcar" <i.uc...@gmail.com>
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> wrote:
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> Actually the current CRAN version (3.2.1) does NOT give
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> correct results either, sorry. It's the release 3.1.2 which gives the
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> correct results.
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> 2016-06-26 9:12 GMT+02:00 Iñaki Úcar <i.uc...@gmail.com>:
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> It seems there's a bug in the development version. The
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> version on CRAN gives correct results though. It would be great if you could
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> reproduce this problem with a much simpler example. It would help me debug
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> the issue.
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> 2016-06-26 6:53 GMT+02:00 moko kamello
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> <mokoka...@gmail.com>:
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> I don't know if this is my bad: the waiting time is
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> positive only if in case of get_mon_arrival(env, per_resources=F)
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> However, It gives me mixed positive and negative values
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> in case of per_resource=T and I have absolutely no clue why this happens
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> Any Help ?
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> On 20 June 2016 at 10:34, Iñaki Úcar <i.uc...@gmail.com>
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> wrote:
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> 2016-06-18 1:05 GMT+02:00 moko kamello
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> <mokoka...@gmail.com>:
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> Is it possible that "waiting time" be negative values ?
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> No, it's not.
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> Iñaki

in get_mon_resources(env, per_resource=T) i see only finished=TRUE. Is
there a way to get the finished=FALSE?

On 29 June 2016 at 14:08, moko kamello <mokoka...@gmail.com> wrote:
> Congratulations for

messages.subject: Re: [simmer-devel] need your opinion: cancer center scenario
messages.subject_clean: [simmer-devel] need your opinion: cancer center scenario
messages.body_plain:
get_mon_resources does NOT have a per_resource argument nor a finished column in the resulting data frame.
get_mon_arrivals does have a per_resource argument, but
per_resource=F (default) shows a finished column, and you’ll see TRUEs and FALSEs.
per_resource=T does NOT show a finished column.
​

messages.body_plain:
Thanks, but I always have "TRUE" only. If for example 200 patients generated I only have 160-170 records with finished= "true" but zero records with finished= false

On Jun 30, 2016 11:41 AM, "Iñaki Úcar" <i.uc...@gmail.com> wrote:

> get_mon_resources does NOT have a per_resource argument nor a finished column in the resulting data frame.
> get_mon_arrivals does have a per_resource argument, but
> per_resource=F (default) shows a finished column, and you’ll see TRUEs and FALSEs.
> per_resource=T does NOT show a finished column.
> ​
>
> 2016-06-30 5:32 GMT+02:00 moko kamello <mokoka...@gmail.com>:
> > in get_mon_resources(env, per_resource=T) i see only finished=TRUE. Is
> > there a way to get the finished=FALSE?
> >
> > On 29 June 2016 at 14:08, moko kamello <mokoka...@gmail.com> wrote:
> > > Congratulations for version 3.3 btw
> > >
> > > On Jun 29, 2016 2:01 PM, "Iñaki Úcar" <i.uc...@gmail.com> wrote:
> > >>
> > >> I was talking about the points in your trajectory, at the end of each
> > >> stage, where a patient may leave with some probability. The case you mention
> > >> is different, of course.
> > >>
> > >> 2016-06-28 21:33 GMT+02:00 moko kamello <mokoka...@gmail.com>:
> > >>>
> > >>> OK, I see. But I think that leave() cannot be used if I want the two
> > >>> branches to seize the resources at different priorities and timeouts for
> > >>> example ..
> > >>>
> > >>>  branch(function() sample(c(1,2),size=1,replace=T,prob=c(0.2,0.8)),
> > >>> merge=c(T, T),
> > >>>                                             create_trajectory("relapse")
> > >>> %>%
> > >>>                                             seize("bed", amount = 1,
> > >>> priority = 1) %>%
> > >>>                                             seize("relapse", amount = 1,
> > >>> priority = 1) %>%
> > >>>                                             timeout(function() rnorm(1,
> > >>> 40, 2)) %>%
> > >>>                                             release("bed", 1)
> > >>>                                                ,
> > >>>
> > >>>
> > >>> create_trajectory("relapse_out") %>%
> > >>>                                              seize("bed", amount = 1,
> > >>> priority = 9) %>%
> > >>>                                              seize("relapse_out", amount
> > >>> = 1, priority = 1)  %>%
> > >>>                                              timeout(function() rnorm(1,
> > >>> 10, 2)) %>%
> > >>>                                              release("bed", 1)
> > >>>
> > >>>                                       )
> > >>>
> > >>> So, in such case there is no other option but to use branch inside a
> > >>> branch, right?
> > >>>
> > >>>
> > >>> On 28 June 2016 at 11:26, Iñaki Úcar <i.uc...@gmail.com> wrote:
> > >>>>
> > >>>> See the associated issue: https://github.com/r-simmer/simmer/issues/63
> > >>>>
> > >>>> 2016-06-28 11:24 GMT+02:00 moko kamello <mokoka...@gmail.com>:
> > >>>>>
> > >>>>> Have any sample ?
> > >>>>>
> > >>>>> On Jun 28, 2016 11:19 AM, "Iñaki Úcar" <i.uc...@gmail.com> wrote:
> > >>>>>>
> > >>>>>> BTW, in order to avoid so many nested branches in your model, you’ll
> > >>>>>> be probably interested in the new activity called leave, which does exactly
> > >>>>>> what you need: leave a trajectory with some probability.
> > >>>>>>
> > >>>>>>
> > >>>>>> 2016-06-27 19:53 GMT+02:00 Iñaki Úcar <i.uc...@gmail.com>:
> > >>>>>>>
> > >>>>>>> The bug is already fixed. Check out the master branch on GitHub. The
> > >>>>>>> CRAN version has the bug and does NOT work properly.
> > >>>>>>>
> > >>>>>>> 2016-06-27 18:55 GMT+02:00 moko kamello <mokoka...@gmail.com>:
> > >>>>>>>>
> > >>>>>>>> For a reason or another the only version working is the one on CRAN.
> > >>>>>>>> Is there any snippet of script to prevent cumulative sum of timeout inside a
> > >>>>>>>> branch
> > >>>>>>>>
> > >>>>>>>> On Jun 27, 2016 4:10 AM, "moko kamello" <mokoka...@gmail.com>
> > >>>>>>>> wrote:
> > >>>>>>>>>
> > >>>>>>>>> Attached simpler example with cummulative time calculated for a
> > >>>>>>>>> branch
> > >>>>>>>>>
> > >>>>>>>>> On 27 June 2016 at 03:45, moko kamello <mokoka...@gmail.com>
> > >>>>>>>>> wrote:
> > >>>>>>>>>>
> > >>>>>>>>>> Now, using the latest CRAN version, I think the error results from
> > >>>>>>>>>> the cumulative sum of time within each branch, this will result in activity
> > >>>>>>>>>> time to become greater and lead to -ve values. Just an opinion.
> > >>>>>>>>>>
> > >>>>>>>>>> On 26 June 2016 at 22:58, Iñaki Úcar <i.uc...@gmail.com> wrote:
> > >>>>>>>>>>>
> > >>>>>>>>>>> Use the version 3.1.2.
> > >>>>>>>>>>>
> > >>>>>>>>>>> 2016-06-26 22:54 GMT+02:00 moko kamello <mokoka...@gmail.com>:
> > >>>>>>>>>>>>
> > >>>>>>>>>>>> Is there any quick work around until this issue is resolved ?
> > >>>>>>>>>>>>
> > >>>>>>>>>>>> On 26 June 2016 at 10:00, Iñaki Úcar <i.uc...@gmail.com> wrote:
> > >>>>>>>>>>>>>
> > >>>>>>>>>>>>> I've opened an issue on GitHub. If anyone finds a smaller piece
> > >>>>>>>>>>>>> of code featuring this bug, please, post it there.
> > >>>>>>>>>>>>>
> > >>>>>>>>>>>>> 2016-06-26 9:42 GMT+02:00 moko kamello
> > >>>>>>>>>>>>> <mokoka...@gmail.com>:
> > >>>>>>>>>>>>>>
> > >>>>>>>>>>>>>> Thanks
> > >>>>>>>>>>>>>>
> > >>>>>>>>>>>>>> On Jun 26, 2016 9:39 AM, "Iñaki Úcar" <i.uc...@gmail.com>
> > >>>>>>>>>>>>>> wrote:
> > >>>>>>>>>>>>>>>
> > >>>>>>>>>>>>>>> You can download every release from the Releases page:

> > >>>>>>>>>>>>>>>
> > >>>>>>>>>>>>>>> 2016-06-26 9:33 GMT+02:00 moko kamello
> > >>>>>>>>>>>>>>> <mokoka...@gmail.com>:
> > >>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>
> > >>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> Could you please send me a zip file to install it as I have
> > >>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> no experience to install it from github
> > >>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>
> > >>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> On Jun 26, 2016 9:28 AM, "Iñaki Úcar" <i.uc...@gmail.com>
> > >>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> wrote:
> > >>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>
> > >>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> Actually the current CRAN version (3.2.1) does NOT give

> > >>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> correct results.
> > >>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>
> > >>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> 2016-06-26 9:12 GMT+02:00 Iñaki Úcar <i.uc...@gmail.com>:
> > >>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>
> > >>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> It seems there's a bug in the development version. The
> > >>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> version on CRAN gives correct results though. It would be great if you could
> > >>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> reproduce this problem with a much simpler example. It would help me debug
> > >>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> the issue.
> > >>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>
> > >>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> 2016-06-26 6:53 GMT+02:00 moko kamello
> > >>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> <mokoka...@gmail.com>:
> > >>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>
> > >>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> I don't know if this is my bad: the waiting time is
> > >>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> positive only if in case of get_mon_arrival(env, per_resources=F)
> > >>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> However, It gives me mixed positive and negative values
> > >>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> in case of per_resource=T and I have absolutely no clue why this happens
> > >>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> Any Help ?
> > >>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>
> > >>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> On 20 June 2016 at 10:34, Iñaki Úcar <i.uc...@gmail.com>
> > >>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> wrote:
> > >>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>
> > >>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> 2016-06-18 1:05 GMT+02:00 moko kamello

> > >>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> Is it possible that "waiting time" be negative values ?

> > >>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> No, it's not.

messages.body_plain:
That's because no one got rejected.

2016-06-30 16:47 GMT+02:00 moko kamello <mokoka...@gmail.com>:

> Thanks, but I always have "TRUE" only. If for example 200 patients generated I only have 160-170 records with finished= "true" but zero records with finished= false
> On Jun 30, 2016 11:41 AM, "Iñaki Úcar" <i.uc...@gmail.com> wrote:
> > get_mon_resources does NOT have a per_resource argument nor a finished column in the resulting data frame.
> > get_mon_arrivals does have a per_resource argument, but
> > per_resource=F (default) shows a finished column, and you’ll see TRUEs and FALSEs.
> > per_resource=T does NOT show a finished column.
> > ​
> >
> > 2016-06-30 5:32 GMT+02:00 moko kamello <mokoka...@gmail.com>:
> > > in get_mon_resources(env, per_resource=T) i see only finished=TRUE. Is
> > > there a way to get the finished=FALSE?
> > >
> > > On 29 June 2016 at 14:08, moko kamello <mokoka...@gmail.com> wrote:
> > > > Congratulations for version 3.3 btw
> > > >
> > > > On Jun 29, 2016 2:01 PM, "Iñaki Úcar" <i.uc...@gmail.com> wrote:
> > > >>
> > > >> I was talking about the points in your trajectory, at the end of each
> > > >> stage, where a patient may leave with some probability. The case you mention
> > > >> is different, of course.
> > > >>
> > > >> 2016-06-28 21:33 GMT+02:00 moko kamello <mokoka...@gmail.com>:
> > > >>>
> > > >>> OK, I see. But I think that leave() cannot be used if I want the two
> > > >>> branches to seize the resources at different priorities and timeouts for
> > > >>> example ..
> > > >>>
> > > >>>  branch(function() sample(c(1,2),size=1,replace=T,prob=c(0.2,0.8)),
> > > >>> merge=c(T, T),
> > > >>>                                             create_trajectory("relapse")
> > > >>> %>%
> > > >>>                                             seize("bed", amount = 1,
> > > >>> priority = 1) %>%
> > > >>>                                             seize("relapse", amount = 1,
> > > >>> priority = 1) %>%
> > > >>>                                             timeout(function() rnorm(1,
> > > >>> 40, 2)) %>%
> > > >>>                                             release("bed", 1)
> > > >>>                                                ,
> > > >>>
> > > >>>
> > > >>> create_trajectory("relapse_out") %>%
> > > >>>                                              seize("bed", amount = 1,
> > > >>> priority = 9) %>%
> > > >>>                                              seize("relapse_out", amount
> > > >>> = 1, priority = 1)  %>%
> > > >>>                                              timeout(function() rnorm(1,
> > > >>> 10, 2)) %>%
> > > >>>                                              release("bed", 1)
> > > >>>
> > > >>>                                       )
> > > >>>
> > > >>> So, in such case there is no other option but to use branch inside a
> > > >>> branch, right?
> > > >>>
> > > >>>
> > > >>> On 28 June 2016 at 11:26, Iñaki Úcar <i.uc...@gmail.com> wrote:
> > > >>>>
> > > >>>> See the associated issue: https://github.com/r-simmer/simmer/issues/63
> > > >>>>
> > > >>>> 2016-06-28 11:24 GMT+02:00 moko kamello <mokoka...@gmail.com>:
> > > >>>>>
> > > >>>>> Have any sample ?
> > > >>>>>
> > > >>>>> On Jun 28, 2016 11:19 AM, "Iñaki Úcar" <i.uc...@gmail.com> wrote:
> > > >>>>>>
> > > >>>>>> BTW, in order to avoid so many nested branches in your model, you’ll
> > > >>>>>> be probably interested in the new activity called leave, which does exactly
> > > >>>>>> what you need: leave a trajectory with some probability.
> > > >>>>>>
> > > >>>>>>
> > > >>>>>> 2016-06-27 19:53 GMT+02:00 Iñaki Úcar <i.uc...@gmail.com>:
> > > >>>>>>>
> > > >>>>>>> The bug is already fixed. Check out the master branch on GitHub. The
> > > >>>>>>> CRAN version has the bug and does NOT work properly.
> > > >>>>>>>
> > > >>>>>>> 2016-06-27 18:55 GMT+02:00 moko kamello <mokoka...@gmail.com>:
> > > >>>>>>>>
> > > >>>>>>>> For a reason or another the only version working is the one on CRAN.
> > > >>>>>>>> Is there any snippet of script to prevent cumulative sum of timeout inside a
> > > >>>>>>>> branch
> > > >>>>>>>>
> > > >>>>>>>> On Jun 27, 2016 4:10 AM, "moko kamello" <mokoka...@gmail.com>
> > > >>>>>>>> wrote:
> > > >>>>>>>>>
> > > >>>>>>>>> Attached simpler example with cummulative time calculated for a
> > > >>>>>>>>> branch
> > > >>>>>>>>>
> > > >>>>>>>>> On 27 June 2016 at 03:45, moko kamello <mokoka...@gmail.com>
> > > >>>>>>>>> wrote:
> > > >>>>>>>>>>
> > > >>>>>>>>>> Now, using the latest CRAN version, I think the error results from
> > > >>>>>>>>>> the cumulative sum of time within each branch, this will result in activity
> > > >>>>>>>>>> time to become greater and lead to -ve values. Just an opinion.
> > > >>>>>>>>>>
> > > >>>>>>>>>> On 26 June 2016 at 22:58, Iñaki Úcar <i.uc...@gmail.com> wrote:
> > > >>>>>>>>>>>
> > > >>>>>>>>>>> Use the version 3.1.2.
> > > >>>>>>>>>>>
> > > >>>>>>>>>>> 2016-06-26 22:54 GMT+02:00 moko kamello <mokoka...@gmail.com>:

> > > >>>>>>>>>>>> Is there any quick work around until this issue is resolved ?
> > > >>>>>>>>>>>>

> > > >>>>>>>>>>>>>
> > > >>>>>>>>>>>>> I've opened an issue on GitHub. If anyone finds a smaller piece
> > > >>>>>>>>>>>>> of code featuring this bug, please, post it there.
> > > >>>>>>>>>>>>>

> > > >>>>>>>>>>>>>> Thanks
> > > >>>>>>>>>>>>>>

> > > >>>>>>>>>>>>>>> You can download every release from the Releases page:

> > > >>>>>>>>>>>>>>>
> > > >>>>>>>>>>>>>>> 2016-06-26 9:33 GMT+02:00 moko kamello
> > > >>>>>>>>>>>>>>> <mokoka...@gmail.com>:
> > > >>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>
> > > >>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> Could you please send me a zip file to install it as I have
> > > >>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> no experience to install it from github
> > > >>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>
> > > >>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> On Jun 26, 2016 9:28 AM, "Iñaki Úcar" <i.uc...@gmail.com>
> > > >>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> wrote:
> > > >>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>
> > > >>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> Actually the current CRAN version (3.2.1) does NOT give
> > > >>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> correct results either, sorry. It's the release 3.1.2 which gives the
> > > >>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> correct results.
> > > >>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>
> > > >>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> 2016-06-26 9:12 GMT+02:00 Iñaki Úcar <i.uc...@gmail.com>:

> > > >>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> It seems there's a bug in the development version. The

> > > >>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> the issue.
> > > >>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>
> > > >>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> 2016-06-26 6:53 GMT+02:00 moko kamello
> > > >>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> <mokoka...@gmail.com>:
> > > >>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>
> > > >>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> I don't know if this is my bad: the waiting time is

> > > >>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> However, It gives me mixed positive and negative values
> > > >>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> in case of per_resource=T and I have absolutely no clue why this happens
> > > >>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> Any Help ?
> > > >>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>
> > > >>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> On 20 June 2016 at 10:34, Iñaki Úcar <i.uc...@gmail.com>
> > > >>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> wrote:

> > > >>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> 2016-06-18 1:05 GMT+02:00 moko kamello

messages.body_plain:
Sorry for bothering, how can a patient get rejected

On Jun 30, 2016 5:03 PM, "Iñaki Úcar" <i.uc...@gmail.com> wrote:

> That's because no one got rejected.
>
> 2016-06-30 16:47 GMT+02:00 moko kamello <mokoka...@gmail.com>:
> >
> > Thanks, but I always have "TRUE" only. If for example 200 patients generated I only have 160-170 records with finished= "true" but zero records with finished= false
> > On Jun 30, 2016 11:41 AM, "Iñaki Úcar" <i.uc...@gmail.com> wrote:
> > > get_mon_resources does NOT have a per_resource argument nor a finished column in the resulting data frame.
> > > get_mon_arrivals does have a per_resource argument, but
> > > per_resource=F (default) shows a finished column, and you’ll see TRUEs and FALSEs.
> > > per_resource=T does NOT show a finished column.
> > > ​
> > >
> > > 2016-06-30 5:32 GMT+02:00 moko kamello <mokoka...@gmail.com>:
> > > > in get_mon_resources(env, per_resource=T) i see only finished=TRUE. Is
> > > > there a way to get the finished=FALSE?
> > > >
> > > > On 29 June 2016 at 14:08, moko kamello <mokoka...@gmail.com> wrote:
> > > > > Congratulations for version 3.3 btw
> > > > >
> > > > > On Jun 29, 2016 2:01 PM, "Iñaki Úcar" <i.uc...@gmail.com> wrote:
> > > > >>
> > > > >> I was talking about the points in your trajectory, at the end of each
> > > > >> stage, where a patient may leave with some probability. The case you mention
> > > > >> is different, of course.
> > > > >>
> > > > >> 2016-06-28 21:33 GMT+02:00 moko kamello <mokoka...@gmail.com>:
> > > > >>>
> > > > >>> OK, I see. But I think that leave() cannot be used if I want the two
> > > > >>> branches to seize the resources at different priorities and timeouts for
> > > > >>> example ..
> > > > >>>
> > > > >>>  branch(function() sample(c(1,2),size=1,replace=T,prob=c(0.2,0.8)),
> > > > >>> merge=c(T, T),
> > > > >>>                                             create_trajectory("relapse")
> > > > >>> %>%
> > > > >>>                                             seize("bed", amount = 1,
> > > > >>> priority = 1) %>%
> > > > >>>                                             seize("relapse", amount = 1,
> > > > >>> priority = 1) %>%
> > > > >>>                                             timeout(function() rnorm(1,
> > > > >>> 40, 2)) %>%
> > > > >>>                                             release("bed", 1)
> > > > >>>                                                ,
> > > > >>>
> > > > >>>
> > > > >>> create_trajectory("relapse_out") %>%
> > > > >>>                                              seize("bed", amount = 1,
> > > > >>> priority = 9) %>%
> > > > >>>                                              seize("relapse_out", amount
> > > > >>> = 1, priority = 1)  %>%
> > > > >>>                                              timeout(function() rnorm(1,
> > > > >>> 10, 2)) %>%
> > > > >>>                                              release("bed", 1)
> > > > >>>
> > > > >>>                                       )
> > > > >>>
> > > > >>> So, in such case there is no other option but to use branch inside a
> > > > >>> branch, right?
> > > > >>>
> > > > >>>
> > > > >>> On 28 June 2016 at 11:26, Iñaki Úcar <i.uc...@gmail.com> wrote:
> > > > >>>>
> > > > >>>> See the associated issue: https://github.com/r-simmer/simmer/issues/63
> > > > >>>>
> > > > >>>> 2016-06-28 11:24 GMT+02:00 moko kamello <mokoka...@gmail.com>:
> > > > >>>>>
> > > > >>>>> Have any sample ?
> > > > >>>>>
> > > > >>>>> On Jun 28, 2016 11:19 AM, "Iñaki Úcar" <i.uc...@gmail.com> wrote:
> > > > >>>>>>
> > > > >>>>>> BTW, in order to avoid so many nested branches in your model, you’ll
> > > > >>>>>> be probably interested in the new activity called leave, which does exactly
> > > > >>>>>> what you need: leave a trajectory with some probability.
> > > > >>>>>>
> > > > >>>>>>
> > > > >>>>>> 2016-06-27 19:53 GMT+02:00 Iñaki Úcar <i.uc...@gmail.com>:
> > > > >>>>>>>
> > > > >>>>>>> The bug is already fixed. Check out the master branch on GitHub. The
> > > > >>>>>>> CRAN version has the bug and does NOT work properly.
> > > > >>>>>>>
> > > > >>>>>>> 2016-06-27 18:55 GMT+02:00 moko kamello <mokoka...@gmail.com>:
> > > > >>>>>>>>
> > > > >>>>>>>> For a reason or another the only version working is the one on CRAN.
> > > > >>>>>>>> Is there any snippet of script to prevent cumulative sum of timeout inside a
> > > > >>>>>>>> branch
> > > > >>>>>>>>
> > > > >>>>>>>> On Jun 27, 2016 4:10 AM, "moko kamello" <mokoka...@gmail.com>
> > > > >>>>>>>> wrote:
> > > > >>>>>>>>>
> > > > >>>>>>>>> Attached simpler example with cummulative time calculated for a
> > > > >>>>>>>>> branch
> > > > >>>>>>>>>
> > > > >>>>>>>>> On 27 June 2016 at 03:45, moko kamello <mokoka...@gmail.com>
> > > > >>>>>>>>> wrote:
> > > > >>>>>>>>>>
> > > > >>>>>>>>>> Now, using the latest CRAN version, I think the error results from
> > > > >>>>>>>>>> the cumulative sum of time within each branch, this will result in activity
> > > > >>>>>>>>>> time to become greater and lead to -ve values. Just an opinion.
> > > > >>>>>>>>>>
> > > > >>>>>>>>>> On 26 June 2016 at 22:58, Iñaki Úcar <i.uc...@gmail.com> wrote:
> > > > >>>>>>>>>>>
> > > > >>>>>>>>>>> Use the version 3.1.2.
> > > > >>>>>>>>>>>
> > > > >>>>>>>>>>> 2016-06-26 22:54 GMT+02:00 moko kamello <mokoka...@gmail.com>:
> > > > >>>>>>>>>>>>
> > > > >>>>>>>>>>>> Is there any quick work around until this issue is resolved ?
> > > > >>>>>>>>>>>>
> > > > >>>>>>>>>>>> On 26 June 2016 at 10:00, Iñaki Úcar <i.uc...@gmail.com> wrote:
> > > > >>>>>>>>>>>>>
> > > > >>>>>>>>>>>>> I've opened an issue on GitHub. If anyone finds a smaller piece
> > > > >>>>>>>>>>>>> of code featuring this bug, please, post it there.
> > > > >>>>>>>>>>>>>
> > > > >>>>>>>>>>>>> 2016-06-26 9:42 GMT+02:00 moko kamello
> > > > >>>>>>>>>>>>> <mokoka...@gmail.com>:
> > > > >>>>>>>>>>>>>>
> > > > >>>>>>>>>>>>>> Thanks
> > > > >>>>>>>>>>>>>>
> > > > >>>>>>>>>>>>>> On Jun 26, 2016 9:39 AM, "Iñaki Úcar" <i.uc...@gmail.com>
> > > > >>>>>>>>>>>>>> wrote:
> > > > >>>>>>>>>>>>>>>
> > > > >>>>>>>>>>>>>>> You can download every release from the Releases page:
> > > > >>>>>>>>>>>>>>> https://github.com/r-simmer/simmer/releases
> > > > >>>>>>>>>>>>>>>
> > > > >>>>>>>>>>>>>>> 2016-06-26 9:33 GMT+02:00 moko kamello
> > > > >>>>>>>>>>>>>>> <mokoka...@gmail.com>:
> > > > >>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>
> > > > >>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> Could you please send me a zip file to install it as I have
> > > > >>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> no experience to install it from github
> > > > >>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>
> > > > >>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> On Jun 26, 2016 9:28 AM, "Iñaki Úcar" <i.uc...@gmail.com>
> > > > >>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> wrote:
> > > > >>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>
> > > > >>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> Actually the current CRAN version (3.2.1) does NOT give
> > > > >>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> correct results either, sorry. It's the release 3.1.2 which gives the
> > > > >>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> correct results.
> > > > >>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>
> > > > >>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> 2016-06-26 9:12 GMT+02:00 Iñaki Úcar <i.uc...@gmail.com>:
> > > > >>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>
> > > > >>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> It seems there's a bug in the development version. The
> > > > >>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> version on CRAN gives correct results though. It would be great if you could
> > > > >>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> reproduce this problem with a much simpler example. It would help me debug
> > > > >>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> the issue.
> > > > >>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>
> > > > >>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> 2016-06-26 6:53 GMT+02:00 moko kamello
> > > > >>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> <mokoka...@gmail.com>:
> > > > >>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>
> > > > >>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> I don't know if this is my bad: the waiting time is
> > > > >>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> positive only if in case of get_mon_arrival(env, per_resources=F)
> > > > >>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> However, It gives me mixed positive and negative values
> > > > >>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> in case of per_resource=T and I have absolutely no clue why this happens
> > > > >>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> Any Help ?
> > > > >>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>
> > > > >>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> On 20 June 2016 at 10:34, Iñaki Úcar <i.uc...@gmail.com>
> > > > >>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> wrote:
> > > > >>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>
> > > > >>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> 2016-06-18 1:05 GMT+02:00 moko kamello
> > > > >>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> <mokoka...@gmail.com>:
> > > > >>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>
> > > > >>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> Is it possible that "waiting time" be negative values ?
> > > > >>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>
> > > > >>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>
> > > > >>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> No, it's not.
> > > > >>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>
> > > > >>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> Iñaki

Sorry for bothering, how can a patient get rejected

On Jun 30, 2016 5:03 PM, "Iñaki Úcar" <i.uc...@gmail.com> wrote:

> That's because no one got rejected.
>

messages.subject: Re: [simmer-devel] need your opinion: cancer center scenario
messages.subject_clean: [simmer-devel] need your opinion: cancer center scenario
messages.body_plain:
By trying to seize a resource with no space in queue or by using `leave` instead of `branch`. A `branch` is an alternative but perfectly valid trajectory.

2016-06-30 18:08 GMT+02:00 moko kamello <mokoka...@gmail.com>:

> Sorry for bothering, how can a patient get rejected
> On Jun 30, 2016 5:03 PM, "Iñaki Úcar" <i.uc...@gmail.com> wrote:
> > That's because no one got rejected.
> >
> > 2016-06-30 16:47 GMT+02:00 moko kamello <mokoka...@gmail.com>:
> > >
> > > Thanks, but I always have "TRUE" only. If for example 200 patients generated I only have 160-170 records with finished= "true" but zero records with finished= false
> > > On Jun 30, 2016 11:41 AM, "Iñaki Úcar" <i.uc...@gmail.com> wrote:
> > > > get_mon_resources does NOT have a per_resource argument nor a finished column in the resulting data frame.
> > > > get_mon_arrivals does have a per_resource argument, but
> > > > per_resource=F (default) shows a finished column, and you’ll see TRUEs and FALSEs.
> > > > per_resource=T does NOT show a finished column.
> > > > ​
> > > >
> > > > 2016-06-30 5:32 GMT+02:00 moko kamello <mokoka...@gmail.com>:
> > > > > in get_mon_resources(env, per_resource=T) i see only finished=TRUE. Is
> > > > > there a way to get the finished=FALSE?
> > > > >
> > > > > On 29 June 2016 at 14:08, moko kamello <mokoka...@gmail.com> wrote:
> > > > > > Congratulations for version 3.3 btw
> > > > > >
> > > > > > On Jun 29, 2016 2:01 PM, "Iñaki Úcar" <i.uc...@gmail.com> wrote:
> > > > > >>
> > > > > >> I was talking about the points in your trajectory, at the end of each
> > > > > >> stage, where a patient may leave with some probability. The case you mention
> > > > > >> is different, of course.
> > > > > >>
> > > > > >> 2016-06-28 21:33 GMT+02:00 moko kamello <mokoka...@gmail.com>:
> > > > > >>>
> > > > > >>> OK, I see. But I think that leave() cannot be used if I want the two
> > > > > >>> branches to seize the resources at different priorities and timeouts for
> > > > > >>> example ..
> > > > > >>>
> > > > > >>>  branch(function() sample(c(1,2),size=1,replace=T,prob=c(0.2,0.8)),
> > > > > >>> merge=c(T, T),
> > > > > >>>                                             create_trajectory("relapse")
> > > > > >>> %>%
> > > > > >>>                                             seize("bed", amount = 1,
> > > > > >>> priority = 1) %>%
> > > > > >>>                                             seize("relapse", amount = 1,
> > > > > >>> priority = 1) %>%
> > > > > >>>                                             timeout(function() rnorm(1,
> > > > > >>> 40, 2)) %>%
> > > > > >>>                                             release("bed", 1)
> > > > > >>>                                                ,
> > > > > >>>
> > > > > >>>
> > > > > >>> create_trajectory("relapse_out") %>%
> > > > > >>>                                              seize("bed", amount = 1,
> > > > > >>> priority = 9) %>%
> > > > > >>>                                              seize("relapse_out", amount
> > > > > >>> = 1, priority = 1)  %>%
> > > > > >>>                                              timeout(function() rnorm(1,
> > > > > >>> 10, 2)) %>%
> > > > > >>>                                              release("bed", 1)
> > > > > >>>
> > > > > >>>                                       )
> > > > > >>>
> > > > > >>> So, in such case there is no other option but to use branch inside a
> > > > > >>> branch, right?
> > > > > >>>
> > > > > >>>
> > > > > >>> On 28 June 2016 at 11:26, Iñaki Úcar <i.uc...@gmail.com> wrote:
> > > > > >>>>
> > > > > >>>> See the associated issue: https://github.com/r-simmer/simmer/issues/63
> > > > > >>>>
> > > > > >>>> 2016-06-28 11:24 GMT+02:00 moko kamello <mokoka...@gmail.com>:
> > > > > >>>>>
> > > > > >>>>> Have any sample ?
> > > > > >>>>>
> > > > > >>>>> On Jun 28, 2016 11:19 AM, "Iñaki Úcar" <i.uc...@gmail.com> wrote:
> > > > > >>>>>>
> > > > > >>>>>> BTW, in order to avoid so many nested branches in your model, you’ll
> > > > > >>>>>> be probably interested in the new activity called leave, which does exactly
> > > > > >>>>>> what you need: leave a trajectory with some probability.
> > > > > >>>>>>
> > > > > >>>>>>
> > > > > >>>>>> 2016-06-27 19:53 GMT+02:00 Iñaki Úcar <i.uc...@gmail.com>:
> > > > > >>>>>>>
> > > > > >>>>>>> The bug is already fixed. Check out the master branch on GitHub. The
> > > > > >>>>>>> CRAN version has the bug and does NOT work properly.
> > > > > >>>>>>>
> > > > > >>>>>>> 2016-06-27 18:55 GMT+02:00 moko kamello <mokoka...@gmail.com>:
> > > > > >>>>>>>>
> > > > > >>>>>>>> For a reason or another the only version working is the one on CRAN.
> > > > > >>>>>>>> Is there any snippet of script to prevent cumulative sum of timeout inside a
> > > > > >>>>>>>> branch
> > > > > >>>>>>>>
> > > > > >>>>>>>> On Jun 27, 2016 4:10 AM, "moko kamello" <mokoka...@gmail.com>
> > > > > >>>>>>>> wrote:
> > > > > >>>>>>>>>
> > > > > >>>>>>>>> Attached simpler example with cummulative time calculated for a
> > > > > >>>>>>>>> branch
> > > > > >>>>>>>>>
> > > > > >>>>>>>>> On 27 June 2016 at 03:45, moko kamello <mokoka...@gmail.com>
> > > > > >>>>>>>>> wrote:
> > > > > >>>>>>>>>>
> > > > > >>>>>>>>>> Now, using the latest CRAN version, I think the error results from
> > > > > >>>>>>>>>> the cumulative sum of time within each branch, this will result in activity
> > > > > >>>>>>>>>> time to become greater and lead to -ve values. Just an opinion.
> > > > > >>>>>>>>>>
> > > > > >>>>>>>>>> On 26 June 2016 at 22:58, Iñaki Úcar <i.uc...@gmail.com> wrote:
> > > > > >>>>>>>>>>>
> > > > > >>>>>>>>>>> Use the version 3.1.2.
> > > > > >>>>>>>>>>>
> > > > > >>>>>>>>>>> 2016-06-26 22:54 GMT+02:00 moko kamello <mokoka...@gmail.com>:
> > > > > >>>>>>>>>>>>
> > > > > >>>>>>>>>>>> Is there any quick work around until this issue is resolved ?
> > > > > >>>>>>>>>>>>
> > > > > >>>>>>>>>>>> On 26 June 2016 at 10:00, Iñaki Úcar <i.uc...@gmail.com> wrote:
> > > > > >>>>>>>>>>>>>
> > > > > >>>>>>>>>>>>> I've opened an issue on GitHub. If anyone finds a smaller piece
> > > > > >>>>>>>>>>>>> of code featuring this bug, please, post it there.
> > > > > >>>>>>>>>>>>>
> > > > > >>>>>>>>>>>>> 2016-06-26 9:42 GMT+02:00 moko kamello
> > > > > >>>>>>>>>>>>> <mokoka...@gmail.com>:
> > > > > >>>>>>>>>>>>>>
> > > > > >>>>>>>>>>>>>> Thanks
> > > > > >>>>>>>>>>>>>>
> > > > > >>>>>>>>>>>>>> On Jun 26, 2016 9:39 AM, "Iñaki Úcar" <i.uc...@gmail.com>
> > > > > >>>>>>>>>>>>>> wrote:
> > > > > >>>>>>>>>>>>>>>
> > > > > >>>>>>>>>>>>>>> You can download every release from the Releases page:
> > > > > >>>>>>>>>>>>>>> https://github.com/r-simmer/simmer/releases
> > > > > >>>>>>>>>>>>>>>
> > > > > >>>>>>>>>>>>>>> 2016-06-26 9:33 GMT+02:00 moko kamello
> > > > > >>>>>>>>>>>>>>> <mokoka...@gmail.com>:
> > > > > >>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>
> > > > > >>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> Could you please send me a zip file to install it as I have
> > > > > >>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> no experience to install it from github
> > > > > >>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>
> > > > > >>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> On Jun 26, 2016 9:28 AM, "Iñaki Úcar" <i.uc...@gmail.com>
> > > > > >>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> wrote:
> > > > > >>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>
> > > > > >>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> Actually the current CRAN version (3.2.1) does NOT give
> > > > > >>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> correct results either, sorry. It's the release 3.1.2 which gives the
> > > > > >>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> correct results.
> > > > > >>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>
> > > > > >>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> 2016-06-26 9:12 GMT+02:00 Iñaki Úcar <i.uc...@gmail.com>:
> > > > > >>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>
> > > > > >>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> It seems there's a bug in the development version. The
> > > > > >>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> version on CRAN gives correct results though. It would be great if you could
> > > > > >>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> reproduce this problem with a much simpler example. It would help me debug
> > > > > >>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> the issue.
> > > > > >>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>
> > > > > >>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> 2016-06-26 6:53 GMT+02:00 moko kamello
> > > > > >>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> <mokoka...@gmail.com>:
> > > > > >>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>
> > > > > >>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> I don't know if this is my bad: the waiting time is

> > > > > >>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> However, It gives me mixed positive and negative values

> > > > > >>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> Any Help ?
> > > > > >>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>
